      "title": "Implement Discord bot to replace webhook-based notifications",
      "description": "## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

## Existing State

- `ampa/webhook.py` (~347 lines) — `send_webhook()`, `build_payload()`, `build_command_payload()`, `dead_letter()`
- `ampa/scheduler.py` (~3,659 lines) — 8+ inline webhook call sites using `webhook_module.send_webhook()`: `_post_discord()`, `_post_startup_message()`, `_summarize_for_discord()`, command completion, timeout, delegation idle-state, error conditions, delegation report posting
- `ampa/daemon.py` (~281 lines) — heartbeat sending via webhook, `get_env_config()` reads `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`
- `ampa/README.md` (~388 lines) — operator docs referencing `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` extensively
- `ampa/scheduler_schema.md` — scheduler command schema with `discord_label` metadata
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)
- Update `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 and other docs referencing webhook setup
- Add/update tests for bot notification delivery

## Iteration Plan (Epic Children)

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):
- Bot process implementation and supervision
- Notification API / adapter
- Scheduler migration (replace webhook calls)
- Daemon heartbeat migration
- Webhook removal
- Documentation updates
- Testing

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

## Risks & Design Questions

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

### Work items

- **SA-0MLXENM2Q08JOQI3** — *Extract webhook/notification logic into ampa/notifications.py* (open, blocked). Directly blocked by this epic. The notification extraction work is a subset of this epic's v1 scope — the notification API/adapter deliverable subsumes this item's goals. Should be absorbed as a child or closed in favor of v1 children.
- **SA-0MLXEKUGW0IYHTWG** — *Refactor scheduler.py: extract non-scheduling concerns* (open, epic). Parent epic containing SA-0MLXENM2Q08JOQI3. The scheduler migration work in this epic (replacing inline webhook calls) overlaps with the refactoring epic's notification extraction goal. Coordination needed to avoid duplicate effort.
- **SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS** — *AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier* (open). The original daemon notification work item. Heartbeat migration from webhook to bot is explicitly part of v1 scope. This item's remaining work is subsumed by this epic.
- **SA-0MLXEMPQL0MKQ6L2** — *Extract work-item formatting helpers from scheduler* (open). Sibling under the scheduler refactor epic. Touches notification formatting code in scheduler.py that will be migrated to the notification API. Implementation order matters — formatting extraction could simplify or complicate the bot migration depending on sequencing.
- **SA-0MLC7CT4T0KSMUTM** — *Improve scheduler Discord message formatting* (closed). Completed formatting improvements that established the current message structure. The bot must preserve these formatting decisions when migrating notification types.
- **SA-0MLAB9VKQ01ALR3M** — *Resolve duplication daemon.py/scheduler.py* (closed). Completed work that reduced duplication between daemon and scheduler. Informs the consolidation approach for the notification API.
- **SA-0MLPPFNVO1Y7X717** — *Only show delegation report if changed* (closed). Completed conditional logic for delegation report posting. This logic is a notification type that must be migrated to the bot with the same conditional behavior preserved.
- **SA-0MLDIAVFT1805G2L** — *Discord triage-audit summary missing body* (closed). Fixed a bug where triage-audit Discord messages had empty bodies. The fix established the current triage-audit message format that the bot must replicate.
- **SA-0MLC19HMB0S1U1QQ** — *Suppress triage-audit webhook when no items* (closed). Added conditional suppression of triage-audit webhooks. This suppression logic must be preserved when migrating to the bot notification path.
- **SA-0MLHNNSY90TMYQUE** — *Stop Discord Triage Audit message* (closed). Controlled triage-audit Discord message behavior. Related to notification suppression logic that the bot must honor.
- **SA-0ML5E2A2V1YILTVR** — *Automated PM Agent epic* (open, epic). Top-level APMA parent. Context only — this epic is a standalone peer, not a child.

      \"title\": \"Implement Discord bot to replace webhook-based notifications\",
      \"description\": \"## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

## Existing State

- `ampa/webhook.py` (~347 lines) — `send_webhook()`, `build_payload()`, `build_command_payload()`, `dead_letter()`
- `ampa/scheduler.py` (~3,659 lines) — 8+ inline webhook call sites using `webhook_module.send_webhook()`: `_post_discord()`, `_post_startup_message()`, `_summarize_for_discord()`, command completion, timeout, delegation idle-state, error conditions, delegation report posting
- `ampa/daemon.py` (~281 lines) — heartbeat sending via webhook, `get_env_config()` reads `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`
- `ampa/README.md` (~388 lines) — operator docs referencing `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` extensively
- `ampa/scheduler_schema.md` — scheduler command schema with `discord_label` metadata
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):

- Daemon heartbeat migration
- Webhook removal
- Documentation updates
- Testing

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

## Risks & Design Questions

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

## Summary

The Notification API implementation exists in-tree (`ampa/notifications.py`) and implements the socket-backed delivery, dead-letter fallback, and state tracking required by the intake. All eight acceptance criteria are implemented in code; however the work item remains in `in_review` and cannot be closed until the PR/merges and producer review complete.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `ampa/notifications.py` exposes `notify(title, body, message_type)` as the single public entry point | met | `ampa/notifications.py:187` — `def notify(... )` is implemented and exported. |
| 2 | Messages are serialized as JSON and sent to the bot's Unix socket synchronously from calling code | met | `ampa/notifications.py:282` — `line = json.dumps(msg) + "
"` then `sock.sendall(...)` over `AF_UNIX`. |
| 3 | If the Unix socket is unreachable, messages are written to a local dead-letter file (preserving current `dead_letter()` behavior) | met | `ampa/notifications.py:81` — `dead_letter()` implemented to append JSON records to `.worklog/ampa/deadletter.log`. |
| 4 | If Unix socket path is invalid or permission-denied, dead-letter is invoked and the caller does not crash | met | `ampa/notifications.py:305` — catches `FileNotFoundError`/`OSError` and returns False (notify() then dead-letters without raising). |
| 5 | Retry logic: try socket once, on failure dead-letter immediately (bot will be restarted by supervisor) | met | `ampa/notifications.py:271` — single send attempt implemented via `_send_via_socket()` (no retry loop). |
| 6 | All existing message types supported: heartbeat, command, startup, error, triage-audit, delegation, idle-state, session-block | met | `ampa/notifications.py:243` — `msg["message_type"] = message_type` preserves caller-supplied types/state for all message kinds. |
| 7 | Payload format matches what the bot expects (JSON with `title`, `body`, `message_type` at minimum) | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:360` — bot accepts either `{"content": "..."}` or `{"title": "...", "body": "..."}` so notify()'s payload shapes are compatible. |
| 8 | State file tracking (`last_message_ts`, `last_message_type`) preserved for heartbeat suppression logic | met | `ampa/notifications.py:252` — writes `last_message_ts` and `last_message_type` to the state file after notify(). |

No children.

This item cannot be closed: all acceptance criteria are implemented in code, but the work item remains `in_review` and appears to be awaiting PR merge/producer review before it can be closed.

# AMPA Audit Result

## Summary

Scheduler implements process supervision for the Discord bot: it starts the bot, polls and restarts it, tracks the process in instance state, enforces a 3‑strike failure limit, and shuts the bot down on scheduler exit. One acceptance criterion is only partially satisfied because daemon-level code still exits when the bot token is absent, which could cause a crash outside the scheduler path. Therefore the work item cannot be closed yet.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Scheduler starts the bot process on startup if `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is set | met | ampa/scheduler.py:1244 — `self._ensure_bot_running()` is called at scheduler startup |
| 2 | On each scheduler cycle, scheduler checks if bot process is alive (poll PID) | met | ampa/scheduler.py:659 — `_ensure_bot_running()` calls `self._bot_process.poll()` to detect exit |
| 3 | If bot is dead, scheduler restarts it and logs the restart | met | ampa/scheduler.py:664 — logs exited process and ampa/scheduler.py:673 — restarts via `subprocess.Popen([... "ampa.discord_bot"])` |
| 4 | Bot PID is tracked in scheduler instance state | met | ampa/scheduler.py:630 — `self._bot_process` instance attribute holds the subprocess (pid accessible via `.pid`) |
| 5 | If `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is not set, notifications are silently disabled (no crash) | partial | ampa/scheduler.py:649 — `_ensure_bot_running()` returns early when token missing; but ampa/daemon.py:103–108 — `get_env_config()` raises `SystemExit` if token absent (daemon path can exit) |
| 6 | Graceful shutdown: scheduler sends SIGTERM to bot on exit | met | ampa/scheduler.py:743 — `_shutdown_bot()` sends `terminate()` and waits; ampa/scheduler.py:1250 — shutdown handler invokes `_shutdown_bot()` on signals |
| 7 | If bot fails to start 3 consecutive times, supervisor logs an error but does not crash the scheduler | met | ampa/scheduler.py:631–633 — consecutive-failure counter and limit; ampa/scheduler.py:683–691 — increments and logs final error after 3 attempts |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: one acceptance criterion is only partially satisfied because scheduler behavior is correct when the token is absent but `ampa.daemon.get_env_config()` still raises `SystemExit` when `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is unset, which can cause the daemon to exit outside the scheduler supervision path.

Scheduler implements Discord bot process supervision (start, poll, restart, graceful shutdown, and a 3‑strike start limit). Two system-level gaps remain: the bot PID is only tracked in-memory (not persisted to SchedulerStore), and the daemon still raises `SystemExit` when `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is absent. Because of these gaps the work item cannot be closed yet.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Scheduler starts the bot process on startup if `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is set | met | ampa/scheduler.py:673 — starts bot via `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "ampa.discord_bot"])`. |
| 2 | On each scheduler cycle, scheduler checks if bot process is alive (poll PID) | met | ampa/scheduler.py:659 — calls `self._bot_process.poll()` to detect running state. |
| 3 | If bot is dead, scheduler restarts it and logs the restart | met | ampa/scheduler.py:664 — logs exited process; restart via `Popen` at ampa/scheduler.py:673. |
| 4 | Bot PID is tracked in scheduler instance state | partial | ampa/scheduler.py:630 — `self._bot_process` instance attribute holds the subprocess (pid available via `.pid`); no persistence to `SchedulerStore`. |
| 5 | If `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is not set, notifications are silently disabled (no crash) | partial | ampa/scheduler.py:649 — `_ensure_bot_running()` returns early when token missing; ampa/daemon.py:103 — `get_env_config()` raises `SystemExit` when token absent (daemon path can be fatal). |
| 6 | Graceful shutdown: scheduler sends SIGTERM to bot on exit | met | ampa/scheduler.py:743 — `_shutdown_bot()` calls `.terminate()` then waits, falling back to `.kill()` if needed. |
| 7 | If bot fails to start 3 consecutive times, supervisor logs an error but does not crash the scheduler | met | ampa/scheduler.py:683 — increments `_bot_consecutive_failures` and logs giving up after max attempts without raising. |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: 2 acceptance criteria are only partially satisfied — bot PID/state is tracked only in-memory (not persisted to `SchedulerStore`) and the daemon path still exits when `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is unset (ampa/daemon.py:103), which must be addressed before closing.

# AMPA Audit Result

**Audit Result**

- I ran the AMPA audit for work item `SA-0MLYL732S1UCPT73` (Bot Process Supervision). Outcome: scheduler-level supervision is implemented, but the work item cannot be closed — two system-level gaps remain.
- What is implemented (evidence): scheduler starts the bot via `subprocess.Popen` (`ampa/scheduler.py:673`), polls `.poll()` to detect exits (`ampa/scheduler.py:659`), restarts and logs restarts (`ampa/scheduler.py:664, 673`), enforces a 3‑strike start limit (`ampa/scheduler.py:683`), and performs graceful shutdown (`ampa/scheduler.py:743`).
- Outstanding issues blocking close:
  - Bot PID/state is only tracked in memory (instance attribute `self._bot_process`) and is not persisted to the scheduler store — see `ampa/scheduler.py:630`. Acceptance criterion requires persisting to `SchedulerStore`.
  - Daemon startup still treats a missing `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` as fatal (raises `SystemExit`) — see `ampa/daemon.py:~103`. The scheduler correctly gates behavior when the token is absent, but the daemon path can still exit and needs to be tolerant.
- Recommended next steps:
  1) Persist bot PID + minimal metadata to `SchedulerStore` from `ampa/scheduler.py` and read it on startup; add unit tests covering restart/recovery behavior.  
  2) Update `ampa/daemon.get_env_config()` (or the daemon startup flow in `ampa/daemon.py`) to not raise `SystemExit` when `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is unset — log and continue so notifications remain silently disabled.  
  3) After making the two fixes, re-run the audit and then mark `SA-0MLYL732S1UCPT73` ready for final review/close.
- If you want, I can: (1) open a small PR that persists `bot_pid` into `SchedulerStore`, (2) change the daemon token handling to be non-fatal, and (3) add unit tests — tell me which to do first or I can create them in one branch.

# AMPA Audit Result

## Summary

Scheduler implements Discord bot supervision (start, poll, restart, graceful shutdown, and a 3‑strike start limit). One acceptance criterion is partially satisfied: the scheduler disables notifications when the bot token is unset, but the daemon path still treats a missing `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` as fatal (raises SystemExit). Because of this the work item cannot be closed.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Scheduler starts the bot process on startup if `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is set | met | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:91 — starts bot via `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "ampa.discord_bot"])`. |
| 2 | On each scheduler cycle, scheduler checks if bot process is alive (poll PID) | met | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:77 — calls `self._bot_process.poll()` to detect running state. |
| 3 | If bot is dead, scheduler restarts it and logs the restart | met | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:82 — logs exited process and proceeds to restart via Popen. |
| 4 | Bot PID is tracked in scheduler instance state | met | ampa/scheduler.py:287 — `_bot_process` property proxies `self._bot_supervisor._bot_process` (in-memory PID accessible via `.pid`). |
| 5 | If `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is not set, notifications are silently disabled (no crash) | partial | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:67 — `ensure_running()` returns early when token unset; ampa/daemon.py:103 — `get_env_config()` logs error and raises `SystemExit` when token is absent. |
| 6 | Graceful shutdown: scheduler sends SIGTERM to bot on exit | met | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:151 — `_shutdown_bot()` calls `.terminate()`, waits, and falls back to `.kill()` if needed. |
| 7 | If bot fails to start 3 consecutive times, supervisor logs an error but does not crash the scheduler | met | ampa/bot_supervisor.py:107 — increments failure counter and logs giving up after max attempts without raising. |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: 1 acceptance criterion is partially satisfied — the daemon still raises `SystemExit` when `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is unset (ampa/daemon.py:103), while scheduler-level handling is graceful; fix daemon config handling so missing token is a no-op and re-run final verification.

      "description": "## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

## Existing State

- `ampa/webhook.py` (~347 lines) — `send_webhook()`, `build_payload()`, `build_command_payload()`, `dead_letter()`
- `ampa/scheduler.py` (~3,659 lines) — 8+ inline webhook call sites using `webhook_module.send_webhook()`: `_post_discord()`, `_post_startup_message()`, `_summarize_for_discord()`, command completion, timeout, delegation idle-state, error conditions, delegation report posting
- `ampa/daemon.py` (~281 lines) — heartbeat sending via webhook, `get_env_config()` reads `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`
- `ampa/README.md` (~388 lines) — operator docs referencing `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` extensively
- `ampa/scheduler_schema.md` — scheduler command schema with `discord_label` metadata
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)
- Update `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 and other docs referencing webhook setup
- Add/update tests for bot notification delivery

## Iteration Plan (Epic Children)

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):
- Bot process implementation and supervision
- Notification API / adapter
- Scheduler migration (replace webhook calls)
- Daemon heartbeat migration
- Webhook removal
- Documentation updates
- Testing

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

## Risks & Design Questions

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

- **SA-0MLAB9VKQ01ALR3M** — *Resolve duplication daemon.py/scheduler.py* (closed). Completed work that reduced duplication between daemon and scheduler. Informs the consolidation approach for the notification API.
- **SA-0MLPPFNVO1Y7X717** — *Only show delegation report if changed* (closed). Completed conditional logic for delegation report posting. This logic is a notification type that must be migrated to the bot with the same conditional behavior preserved.

      "title": "Implement Discord bot to replace webhook-based notifications",
      "description": "## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

## Existing State

- `ampa/webhook.py` (~347 lines) — `send_webhook()`, `build_payload()`, `build_command_payload()`, `dead_letter()`
- `ampa/scheduler.py` (~3,659 lines) — 8+ inline webhook call sites using `webhook_module.send_webhook()`: `_post_discord()`, `_post_startup_message()`, `_summarize_for_discord()`, command completion, timeout, delegation idle-state, error conditions, delegation report posting
- `ampa/daemon.py` (~281 lines) — heartbeat sending via webhook, `get_env_config()` reads `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`
- `ampa/README.md` (~388 lines) — operator docs referencing `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` extensively
- `ampa/scheduler_schema.md` — scheduler command schema with `discord_label` metadata
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)
- Update `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 and other docs referencing webhook setup
- Add/update tests for bot notification delivery

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

## Risks & Design Questions

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

# AMPA Audit Result

---
## Goal

Replace all legacy webhook call sites in ampa/scheduler.py (and related modules) with the new notification API so the scheduler uses ampa.notifications.notify() (or the agreed notification API) exclusively, remove direct imports of ampa.webhook, preserve message contents and conditional logic, and verify behavioral parity by running the full test-suite. The immediate work item audited is SA-0MLYL7F5H0E9D72U ("Scheduler Webhook Migration").

## Instructions

- Primary acceptance criteria from the work item:
  - Remove all webhook_module.send_webhook() and webhook_module.build_*_payload() calls from scheduler.py.
  - Replace each call site with equivalent notifications.notify() preserving message type, title, body, components, and conditional logic.
  - Refactor or remove _post_discord() and _post_startup_message() so they use the notification API.
  - Keep _summarize_for_discord() as a formatting helper.
  - Ensure no module imports ampa.webhook after migration.
  - Run full test-suite and ensure all tests pass.
- Preserve existing behavior precisely: suppressions, cooldowns, delegation-report-change detection, idle-state suppression, and dead-letter semantics must be preserved.
- Do not close the work item until:
  - The Notification API dependency (SA-0MLYL6TPJ0Z2DK9U) and/or the Discord bot (ancestor epic) is implemented or a compatible local socket/back-end is available.
  - A full test run (CI or local pytest) verifies parity across migrated sites.
- When migrating tests, replace monkeypatches/mocks that previously targeted ampa.webhook with mocks for ampa.notifications (or update them to match the new socket API).

## Discoveries

- I fetched the work item SA-0MLYL7F5H0E9D72U with children/comments. The work item description and acceptance criteria match the migration goals above.
- The audit tool returned many automated audit comments (ampa-scheduler) with mixed snapshots:
  - Some audit comments claim the migration is NOT complete and list unmet criteria: scheduler still imports ampa.webhook, send_webhook occurrences remain, no notifications.notify replacements found, and the work item is blocked by SA-0MLYL6TPJ0Z2DK9U (Notification API).
  - Other audit comments (older snapshots in the worklog) claim the migration WAS implemented (notifications_module present, _post_discord removed, tests passed). The workspace contains multiple such audit comments reflecting different repository snapshots over time.
- I read ampa/scheduler.py (full file). Current contents show:
  - At top-level the file imports "from . import notifications as notifications_module" (so a notifications module is referenced within scheduler.py).
  - Multiple places already call notifications_module.notify(...) (examples: command timeout handling, test-button message, final generic command notification in start_command).
  - The Scheduler delegates delegation orchestration to DelegationOrchestrator and uses _summarize_for_discord() as a helper.
  - There is no _post_discord() definition in the file we inspected; instead, start_command inlines the summarize + notify call.
- Repo-wide greps / worklog data reveal extensive history:
  - ampa/webhook.py exists in the repo and historically provided send_webhook(), build_payload(), dead_letter(), etc.
  - Many worklog comments and other modules (triage_audit.py, daemon.py, session_block.py, tests) historically referenced webhook code; some of those call sites may or may not have been migrated.
  - The audit outputs are large and partially truncated; a saved full tool output file exists (tool_ca2f4b7e2001…).
- The main blocking dependency is the Notification API / Discord bot epic (SA-0MLYL6TPJ0Z2DK9U and SA-0MLXEN5Q91FMXKEB). Some audit comments say these are implemented; others say they are not. This inconsistency must be resolved by checking the current repo state and the presence/behavior of ampa/notifications.py and the bot socket.

## Accomplished

What we did in this session:
- Queried and fetched the work item SA-0MLYL7F5H0E9D72U (wl show ... --children --json) and collected all comments added by the audit agent (ampa-scheduler). The tool output was large and truncated; full output saved to a tool-output file for later review.
- Inspected and read ampa/scheduler.py entirely to confirm current call sites and verify whether notifications.notify() is already used in this copy of the file.
- Ran repo searches (grep) over the workspace/worklog to surface many audit comments and references to webhook/notification helpers and to find instances of _summarize_for_discord usage.
- Noted mixed evidence: scheduler.py uses notifications_module.notify() in many places (time out, test-button, generic notify), indicating partial/complete migration in this working tree; however many worklog/audit comments indicate remaining webhook references elsewhere and/or a blocked Notification API dependency.

Work still in progress / next actions required:
1. Reconcile the contradictory snapshots and determine canonical repo state:
   - Check for existence and contents of ampa/notifications.py and ampa/webhook.py on disk.
   - Grep the codebase for any remaining send_webhook or import of ampa.webhook:
     - grep for patterns: "send_webhook(", "from . import webhook", "import ampa.webhook", "ampa.webhook"
2. Verify Notification API availability:
   - If ampa/notifications.py exists, inspect its implementation (socket client, dead-letter behavior).
   - If it does not exist or is incomplete, implement or land a minimal notifications.notify() wrapper that meets acceptance criteria (sends JSON over unix socket, dead-letters on failure, preserves last_message_ts/state where required).
3. Update code or tests:
   - If there are remaining call sites using ampa.webhook, migrate them to notifications.notify() and preserve payload builders (or forward pre-built payloads).
   - Update tests to monkeypatch ampa.notifications.notify instead of ampa.webhook, or provide a shim compatibility layer while migrating tests.
4. Run the full test-suite (pytest) and record results; fix any regressions.
5. Once migration and tests are green, remove ampa/webhook.py (only after ensuring no tests or modules import it).
6. Update work item SA-0MLYL7F5H0E9D72U comments to reflect final status and close when criteria met.

Blockers / risks:
- Conflicting audit snapshots in the worklog must be reconciled with the working tree; this is why a repo-wide search for webhook references and checking ampa/notifications.py is critical.
- The Notification API / Discord bot process and its socket protocol are upstream dependencies; if those are not available, the notification API must provide a robust dead-letter fallback so production behavior is not lost.
- Tests currently mock webhook behavior in many places; migration requires updating many test mocks.

## Relevant files / directories (read / examined / referenced)

- Files read directly:
  - ampa/scheduler.py — full file read and analyzed (lines 1–877). Key observations: imports notifications as notifications_module; many notify() calls present; _summarize_for_discord() referenced; start_command inlines notify; run_shell timeout handler calls notifications_module.notify on timeout; test-button message uses notifications_module.notify.
- Files / modules referenced in audits / worklog (need inspection or migration):
  - ampa/webhook.py — legacy webhook helper (send_webhook, build_payload, build_command_payload, dead_letter). Present in repo and referenced by many historical call sites.
  - ampa/delegation.py — delegation orchestration and _summarize_for_discord() helper. Present; scheduler delegates to DelegationOrchestrator.
  - ampa/triage_audit.py — contains notification call sites for triage; may contain webhook-based or notifications-based calls depending on snapshot.
  - ampa/daemon.py — heartbeat sender (historically used webhook); needs to be checked for migration to notifications.notify.
  - ampa/session_block.py — surfaced waiting-for-input notifications; historically used webhook, may need migration.
  - ampa/bot_supervisor.py — manages bot process; referenced by scheduler and may use notifications paths.
  - ampa/notifications.py — (target API). Need to check whether this file exists and its implementation. If missing, implement it.
- Tests that will require updates/inspection:
  - tests/test_notifications.py — unit tests for the notification API; present and referenced in audit comments.
  - tests/test_triage_audit.py — uses webhook mocks; will need to be updated if migration changes API.
  - tests/test_conversation_manager.py — exercises waiting-for-input notifications (may reference webhook).
  - tests/test_hung_child_recovery.py — contains tests that assert notifications for timeouts.

  - .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl — contains many audit comments by ampa-scheduler showing mixed migration status (useful for history).
  - /home/rogardle/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/tool_ca2f4b7e2001X2BwbDBmP06c3o — full saved tool output from the wl show run (contains truncated audit data).

      "description": "## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)
- Update `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 and other docs referencing webhook setup
- Add/update tests for bot notification delivery

## Iteration Plan (Epic Children)

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):
- Bot process implementation and supervision
- Notification API / adapter
- Scheduler migration (replace webhook calls)
- Daemon heartbeat migration
- Webhook removal
- Documentation updates

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

- **SA-0MLPPFNVO1Y7X717** — *Only show delegation report if changed* (closed). Completed conditional logic for delegation report posting. This logic is a notification type that must be migrated to the bot with the same conditional behavior preserved.

      "id": "SA-0MLXEN5Q91FMXKEB",
      "title": "Implement Discord bot to replace webhook-based notifications",
      "description": "## Problem Statement

Replace the current webhook-based Discord notification system with a Discord bot. The existing system uses `ampa/webhook.py` (`send_webhook`, `build_payload`, `build_command_payload`, `dead_letter`) and ~200 lines of inline webhook calls scattered across 8+ locations in `ampa/scheduler.py`, plus heartbeat sending in `ampa/daemon.py`. These webhook calls are one-way, tightly coupled, and duplicated. A Discord bot consolidates all notification delivery into a single supervised process, enables richer message formats, and lays the groundwork for future bidirectional features (slash commands, interactive buttons).

## Users

- Operators running AMPA who need visibility into scheduler activity, command results, delegation reports, triage-audit summaries, and agent liveness via Discord.
- Maintainers who need a clean notification API so they can evolve notification behavior without modifying scheduler, delegation, or triage-audit code.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want a Discord bot that sends all the same notifications I currently receive via webhooks, so I can configure a bot token instead of a webhook URL and receive the same information.
- As an operator, I want the bot to send heartbeat messages at a configurable interval so I can confirm the system is alive without a separate webhook path.
- As a maintainer, I want all Discord notification logic consolidated behind a single bot module so I can add new notification types or change formatting without touching scheduler or daemon code.

## Success Criteria (v1 — notifications only)

- [ ] A Discord bot process implemented using `discord.py` that connects to a configured server and channel
- [ ] The bot sends all notification types currently handled by webhook calls: command completion, timeout, triage-audit summary, delegation idle-state, scheduler startup, error conditions, pre/post dispatch, and delegation report
- [ ] Heartbeat messages currently sent by `ampa/daemon.py` via webhook are sent through the bot instead
- [ ] A clean public notification API (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py` or equivalent) that other modules call instead of `webhook_module.send_webhook`
- [ ] Informational messages use Discord markdown; interactive messages (future versions) will use embeds
- [ ] Single-channel routing for v1; multi-channel routing deferred
- [ ] Bot token configuration via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` (operator creates bot in Discord Developer Portal, copies token, stores in `.env`)
- [ ] Bot token setup documented in `ampa/README.md` with clear instructions for Discord Developer Portal setup
- [ ] Webhook support fully removed once bot is deployed — no fallback/transition period
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover bot notification delivery

## Constraints

- v1 is notifications only. Slash commands, interactive buttons, message threading, multi-channel routing, and status presence are deferred to v2+.
- Runtime: bot runs as a separate process. The scheduler has a command that ensures the bot is up and running. The scheduler spawns and supervises the bot process (similar to how `daemon.py` manages the scheduler).
- Python 3.12+, `discord.py` library.
- Bot token must be supplied via env var `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not commit secrets.
- Single channel for v1, configured via env var or bot config.
- Webhook support is removed entirely — no dual-mode / fallback.

## Existing State

- `ampa/webhook.py` (~347 lines) — `send_webhook()`, `build_payload()`, `build_command_payload()`, `dead_letter()`
- `ampa/scheduler.py` (~3,659 lines) — 8+ inline webhook call sites using `webhook_module.send_webhook()`: `_post_discord()`, `_post_startup_message()`, `_summarize_for_discord()`, command completion, timeout, delegation idle-state, error conditions, delegation report posting
- `ampa/daemon.py` (~281 lines) — heartbeat sending via webhook, `get_env_config()` reads `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`
- `ampa/README.md` (~388 lines) — operator docs referencing `AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` extensively
- `ampa/scheduler_schema.md` — scheduler command schema with `discord_label` metadata
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 — Discord Notifications specification
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — delegation report Discord posting
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — triage-audit Discord summary webhook

## Desired Change

- Implement a Discord bot module (e.g., `ampa/discord_bot.py`) that:
  - Connects to Discord using `discord.py` with a bot token from `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
  - Sends messages to a single configured channel
  - Exposes a notification API (function calls or IPC) that scheduler and daemon code can use to send messages
- Implement a notification adapter (e.g., `ampa/notifications.py`) that:
  - Provides a clean public API replacing all direct `webhook_module.send_webhook()` calls
  - Routes messages to the bot process
  - Preserves all existing message types and content
- Update `ampa/scheduler.py` to call the notification API instead of inline webhook calls
- Update `ampa/daemon.py` to send heartbeats through the bot instead of direct webhook POST
- Remove `ampa/webhook.py` (or gut it to a stub if needed for transition)
- Update `ampa/README.md` with bot token setup instructions (Discord Developer Portal flow, env var, permissions)
- Update `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` section 7.3 and other docs referencing webhook setup
- Add/update tests for bot notification delivery

## Iteration Plan (Epic Children)

**v1: Notifications only** — replace all webhook notifications with bot-sent messages (this intake's scope):
- Bot process implementation and supervision
- Notification API / adapter
- Scheduler migration (replace webhook calls)
- Daemon heartbeat migration
- Webhook removal
- Documentation updates
- Testing

**v2+: Interactive features** (future, separate children):
- Slash commands (`/ampa status`, `/ampa delegate`, `/ampa audit`)
- Interactive buttons/menus for delegation approval
- Multi-channel routing
- Message threading for related events
- Status presence (online/idle/busy)

## Risks & Design Questions

- **Async/sync boundary**: `discord.py` is async; scheduler and daemon are synchronous. The IPC mechanism between sync callers and the async bot process needs design (options: message queue, Unix socket, subprocess stdin, shared file). Key design decision for v1.
- **Bot process resilience**: if the bot process crashes, notifications are lost until it restarts. Need equivalent of the existing `dead_letter()` function — queue unsent messages and retry on reconnect.
- **Channel ID configuration**: besides the bot token, the target channel ID must be configured (env var or discoverable by channel name).
- **Permission scope**: the bot needs `Send Messages` permission at minimum. If embeds are used in v2, `Embed Links` permission will also be needed.

- **SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS** — *AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier* (open). The original daemon notification work item. Heartbeat migration from webhook to bot is explicitly part of v1 scope. This item's remaining work is subsumed by this epic.

Implementation order matters — formatting extraction could simplify or complicate the bot migration depending on sequencing.
- **SA-0MLC7CT4T0KSMUTM** — *Improve scheduler Discord message formatting* (closed). Completed formatting improvements that established the current message structure. The bot must preserve these formatting decisions when migrating notification types.
- **SA-0MLAB9VKQ01ALR3M** — *Resolve duplication daemon.py/scheduler.py* (closed). Completed work that reduced duplication between daemon and scheduler. Informs the consolidation approach for the notification API.
- **SA-0MLPPFNVO1Y7X717** — *Only show delegation report if changed* (closed). Completed conditional logic for delegation report posting. This logic is a notification type that must be migrated to the bot with the same conditional behavior preserved.

      "title": "Full suite of tests is too slow",
      "description": "## Full suite of tests is too slow

### Problem
The full test suite (569 tests across 37 files) hangs indefinitely in CI and locally due to environment variable contamination introduced by `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py`. Three tests hang forever because `load_dotenv(override=True)` leaks `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` into the process environment and `monkeypatch` does not clean it up. Additionally, there is no timeout protection at either the test or CI level, so a single hanging test blocks the entire suite indefinitely.

Secondary issues include 7 leaked HTTP server threads from `test_metrics_and_health.py`, a pre-existing assertion failure in `test_triage_audit.py`, and a slow cleanup integration test (3.52s).

### User Story
As a developer, I want the full test suite to run to completion reliably in under 30 seconds, with timeout protection to prevent future hangs, so that CI feedback is fast and trustworthy.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Environment contamination**: `test_per_project_isolation.py` calls `load_dotenv(override=True)` which sets `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` in `os.environ`. `monkeypatch` only restores values it explicitly patches — it does not undo side effects of `load_dotenv`. Downstream tests (`test_scheduler_run`, `test_scheduler_scoring`, `test_stale_delegation_watchdog`) read the leaked var and enter unexpected code paths that hang.
2. **No timeout protection**: No `pytest-timeout` plugin, no per-test timeouts, no CI job-level `timeout-minutes`.
3. **Thread leaks**: `test_metrics_and_health.py` starts HTTP servers but never shuts them down.
4. **Pre-existing failure**: `test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body` has an assertion mismatch unrelated to performance.

### Scope
- Fix environment contamination in `test_per_project_isolation.py`
- Add `pytest-timeout` as a dev dependency with a sensible default (e.g., 30s per test)
- Add CI-level `timeout-minutes` to both CI jobs
- Fix leaked HTTP server threads in `test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Fix pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py`
- Investigate and if warranted optimise the slow cleanup integration test

### Out of Scope
- Test parallelisation (`pytest-xdist`) — not needed for the <30s target
- Major test architecture refactoring
- Adding new tests (beyond fixing existing ones)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. All 569 tests pass with `pytest -q` (no hangs, no failures, no errors)
2. Full suite completes in under 30 seconds locally
3. `pytest-timeout` is installed as a dev dependency with a default timeout configured in `pyproject.toml`
4. CI jobs have `timeout-minutes` configured
5. No leaked HTTP server threads after test suite completion
6. The pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py` is fixed
7. No environment variable contamination between test files

### Technical References
- Contamination source: `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py` (all test classes using `load_dotenv`)
- Hanging tests: `tests/test_scheduler_run.py::test_cli_run_success`, `tests/test_scheduler_scoring.py::test_scheduler_runs_commands_from_start_cwd`, `tests/test_stale_delegation_watchdog.py::TestStaleDelegationDetection::test_detects_stale_item_beyond_threshold`
- Thread leaks: `tests/test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Slow test: `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (3.52s)
- Pre-existing failure: `tests/test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body`
- CI config: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Pytest config: `pyproject.toml`",

      "description": "## Full suite of tests is too slow

### Problem
The full test suite (569 tests across 37 files) hangs indefinitely in CI and locally due to environment variable contamination introduced by `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py`. Three tests hang forever because `load_dotenv(override=True)` leaks `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` into the process environment and `monkeypatch` does not clean it up. Additionally, there is no timeout protection at either the test or CI level, so a single hanging test blocks the entire suite indefinitely.

Secondary issues include 7 leaked HTTP server threads from `test_metrics_and_health.py`, a pre-existing assertion failure in `test_triage_audit.py`, and a slow cleanup integration test (3.52s).

### User Story
As a developer, I want the full test suite to run to completion reliably in under 30 seconds, with timeout protection to prevent future hangs, so that CI feedback is fast and trustworthy.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Environment contamination**: `test_per_project_isolation.py` calls `load_dotenv(override=True)` which sets `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` in `os.environ`. `monkeypatch` only restores values it explicitly patches — it does not undo side effects of `load_dotenv`. Downstream tests (`test_scheduler_run`, `test_scheduler_scoring`, `test_stale_delegation_watchdog`) read the leaked var and enter unexpected code paths that hang.
2. **No timeout protection**: No `pytest-timeout` plugin, no per-test timeouts, no CI job-level `timeout-minutes`.
3. **Thread leaks**: `test_metrics_and_health.py` starts HTTP servers but never shuts them down.
4. **Pre-existing failure**: `test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body` has an assertion mismatch unrelated to performance.

### Scope
- Fix environment contamination in `test_per_project_isolation.py`
- Add `pytest-timeout` as a dev dependency with a sensible default (e.g., 30s per test)
- Add CI-level `timeout-minutes` to both CI jobs
- Fix leaked HTTP server threads in `test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Fix pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py`
- Investigate and if warranted optimise the slow cleanup integration test

### Out of Scope
- Test parallelisation (`pytest-xdist`) — not needed for the <30s target
- Major test architecture refactoring
- Adding new tests (beyond fixing existing ones)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. All 569 tests pass with `pytest -q` (no hangs, no failures, no errors)
2. Full suite completes in under 30 seconds locally
3. `pytest-timeout` is installed as a dev dependency with a default timeout configured in `pyproject.toml`
4. CI jobs have `timeout-minutes` configured
5. No leaked HTTP server threads after test suite completion
6. The pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py` is fixed
7. No environment variable contamination between test files

### Technical References
- Contamination source: `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py` (all test classes using `load_dotenv`)
- Hanging tests: `tests/test_scheduler_run.py::test_cli_run_success`, `tests/test_scheduler_scoring.py::test_scheduler_runs_commands_from_start_cwd`, `tests/test_stale_delegation_watchdog.py::TestStaleDelegationDetection::test_detects_stale_item_beyond_threshold`
- Thread leaks: `tests/test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Slow test: `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (3.52s)
- Pre-existing failure: `tests/test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body`
- CI config: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Pytest config: `pyproject.toml`",

      \"title\": \"Full suite of tests is too slow\",
      \"description\": \"## Full suite of tests is too slow

### Problem
The full test suite (569 tests across 37 files) hangs indefinitely in CI and locally due to environment variable contamination introduced by `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py`. Three tests hang forever because `load_dotenv(override=True)` leaks `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` into the process environment and `monkeypatch` does not clean it up. Additionally, there is no timeout protection at either the test or CI level, so a single hanging test blocks the entire suite indefinitely.

Secondary issues include 7 leaked HTTP server threads from `test_metrics_and_health.py`, a pre-existing assertion failure in `test_triage_audit.py`, and a slow cleanup integration test (3.52s).

### User Story
As a developer, I want the full test suite to run to completion reliably in under 30 seconds, with timeout protection to prevent future hangs, so that CI feedback is fast and trustworthy.

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Environment contamination**: `test_per_project_isolation.py` calls `load_dotenv(override=True)` which sets `AMPA_PROJECT_DIR` in `os.environ`. `monkeypatch` only restores values it explicitly patches — it does not undo side effects of `load_dotenv`. Downstream tests (`test_scheduler_run`, `test_scheduler_scoring`, `test_stale_delegation_watchdog`) read the leaked var and enter unexpected code paths that hang.
2. **No timeout protection**: No `pytest-timeout` plugin, no per-test timeouts, no CI job-level `timeout-minutes`.
3. **Thread leaks**: `test_metrics_and_health.py` starts HTTP servers but never shuts them down.
4. **Pre-existing failure**: `test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body` has an assertion mismatch unrelated to performance.

### Scope
- Fix environment contamination in `test_per_project_isolation.py`
- Add `pytest-timeout` as a dev dependency with a sensible default (e.g., 30s per test)
- Add CI-level `timeout-minutes` to both CI jobs
- Fix leaked HTTP server threads in `test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Fix pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py`
- Investigate and if warranted optimise the slow cleanup integration test

### Out of Scope
- Test parallelisation (`pytest-xdist`) — not needed for the <30s target
- Major test architecture refactoring
- Adding new tests (beyond fixing existing ones)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. All 569 tests pass with `pytest -q` (no hangs, no failures, no errors)
2. Full suite completes in under 30 seconds locally
3. `pytest-timeout` is installed as a dev dependency with a default timeout configured in `pyproject.toml`
4. CI jobs have `timeout-minutes` configured
5. No leaked HTTP server threads after test suite completion
6. The pre-existing test failure in `test_triage_audit.py` is fixed
7. No environment variable contamination between test files

### Technical References
- Contamination source: `tests/test_per_project_isolation.py` (all test classes using `load_dotenv`)
- Hanging tests: `tests/test_scheduler_run.py::test_cli_run_success`, `tests/test_scheduler_scoring.py::test_scheduler_runs_commands_from_start_cwd`, `tests/test_stale_delegation_watchdog.py::TestStaleDelegationDetection::test_detects_stale_item_beyond_threshold`
- Thread leaks: `tests/test_metrics_and_health.py`
- Slow test: `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (3.52s)
- Pre-existing failure: `tests/test_triage_audit.py::test_triage_audit_discord_summary_includes_body`
- CI config: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Pytest config: `pyproject.toml`\",

# AMPA Audit Result

## Summary

The work item identifies a real false-positive: `_format_in_progress_items()` currently treats non-empty fallback lines (like "No in-progress work items found") as in-progress items. Code review shows the parser correctly finds real `- SA-` lines but the fallback loop (lines 114-118) causes the false-positive. Two acceptance criteria remain unmet; the item cannot be closed yet.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `_format_in_progress_items('')` returns `[]` | met | ampa/delegation.py:104 — splits input with `(text or "").splitlines()`, producing an empty `lines` list for `''` so no items are appended |
| 2 | `_format_in_progress_items('No in-progress work items found')` returns `[]` | unmet | ampa/delegation.py:114 — fallback loop appends any non-empty line (`items.append(stripped)`), so the "No in-progress work items found" line is treated as an item |
| 3 | `_format_in_progress_items('Error: connection refused')` returns `[]` | unmet | ampa/delegation.py:114 — same fallback behavior will append error text as an item rather than returning `[]` |
| 4 | `_format_in_progress_items(text_with_real_SA_items)` returns the correct item lines | met | ampa/delegation.py:110-112 — function filters for lines containing `"- SA-"` and cleans tree characters via `lstrip`, so real SA item lines are captured and normalized |
| 5 | `_build_dry_run_report()` produces idle messaging (not 'busy') when `_format_in_progress_items` returns `[]` | met | ampa/delegation.py:156 — when `in_progress_items` is empty the function builds the full (idle) report with `"- (none)"` and an idle summary |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: 2 acceptance criteria are unmet (criteria 2 and 3 — fallback appends non-item lines). The fix should remove or guard the fallback at `ampa/delegation.py:114-118` so only real `- SA-` lines are returned; after applying that change, add unit tests for the no-items and error-output cases and re-run tests.
