# AMPA Audit Result

## Summary

Implementation for interactive Discord buttons is present: socket `components` handling, `discord.ui.View`/`Button` construction, `on_interaction` acknowledgement, scheduler `test-button` command, tests, and README docs. Two verification gaps remain (no explicit mocked end‑to‑end test asserting `interaction.response.send_message()` and no test/proof of scheduler duplicate‑send/dedup on restart) and two children require producer review, so the item cannot be closed.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Bot sends test message ("Testing interactivity, Blue or Red?") with two clickable `discord.ui.Button` components every 15 minutes via scheduler command | met | `ampa/scheduler.py:481-500` — `_send_test_button_message()` builds components and calls `notifications.notify(...)`. |
| 2 | When a user clicks a button, the bot replies in-channel with an acknowledgement including clicker identity and ISO timestamp | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:265-269` — `ack_message` constructed and `await interaction.response.send_message(ack_message)` invoked. |
| 3 | Unix socket protocol extended with generic `components` field; bot constructs `discord.ui.View`/`discord.ui.Button` objects | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:380-391` — parses `components` and calls `_build_view(components)`. |
| 4 | Button interaction handling plumbing routes through `conversation_manager`/`responder` (MVP no-op) | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:256-257` & `ampa/discord_bot.py:137-144` — `_route_interaction()` invoked and `test_` prefix handled as no-op routing. |
| 5 | Mock-based tests verify: (a) protocol handles component payloads, (b) button construction produces valid `View`/`Button`, and (c) interaction callback handling produces correct acknowledgement format | partial | `tests/test_discord_bot.py:558 & 659` — component/socket and `_build_view` unit tests exist; no mocked end‑to‑end test asserting `interaction.response.send_message()` was called with the ack was found. |
| 6 | Short docs added describing enabling test message, permissions, and component protocol | met | `ampa/README.md:443-486` — `## Interactive Buttons (MVP)` section with protocol example and `notify()` usage. |
| 7 | All existing tests continue to pass; no regressions in notification delivery | partial | `tests/` updated across modules but a full test‑suite/CI run was not executed during this audit to confirm no regressions. |

## Children Status

### Socket Protocol Component Extension (SA-0MM03WPV801P8Q8Z) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Socket accepts optional `components` alongside content/title/body | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:380-384` — `components = data.get("components")` parsed in `_handle_client()`. |
| 2 | Component object shape validated (`type`,`label`,`custom_id`) | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:79-89` — `_validate_components()` enforces required fields and types. |
| 3 | Backward compatibility preserved for payloads without `components` | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:349-370` — content/title/body fallback preserved. |
| 4 | Producer review required on this child | unmet | Worklog metadata/comments indicate `needsProducerReview=true` for SA-0MM03WPV801P8Q8Z. |

### Bot Button Construction and Sending (SA-0MM03X33703438S8) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Construct `discord.ui.View` and `discord.ui.Button` from `components` | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:94-123` — `_build_view()` creates `View` and `Button` instances and adds them. |
| 2 | `View.timeout` set so buttons persist until restart | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:104-107` — `discord.ui.View(timeout=None)` used. |
| 3 | Messages with components sent via `channel.send(content=..., view=...)` | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:429-432` — `_send_to_discord()` includes `view` when present. |

### Button Interaction Handler (SA-0MM03XFHP05MRGCB) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Bot handles `discord.Interaction` events for button clicks | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:235-247` — `on_interaction` registered and component interactions filtered. |
| 2 | Acknowledgement format includes label, user#discriminator, ISO timestamp | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:261-267` — label derived and ack formatted with user and ISO timestamp. |
| 3 | Interaction responded to within 3s (no deferred) | partial | `ampa/discord_bot.py:269` — immediate `interaction.response.send_message(...)` used, but no latency/timeout test exists. |

### Conversation Manager No-Op Wiring (SA-0MM03XTIO01J1MLN) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Interaction handler calls dispatch before acknowledging | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:256-257` — `_route_interaction()` invoked prior to ack. |
| 2 | For `test_*` custom_ids the dispatch is a no-op (MVP) | met | `ampa/discord_bot.py:137-144` — `_route_interaction()` logs and returns for `test_` prefix. |
| 3 | No-op path minimal latency | partial | `ampa/discord_bot.py:126-136` — implementation trivial/non-blocking but no timing test provided. |

### Notification API Component Support (SA-0MM03Y5Y41KUITF7) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `notify()` accepts `components` kwarg and forwards it in socket payload | met | `ampa/notifications.py:187-195 & 241-243` — `notify(..., components=...)` signature and `msg["components"] = components` when provided. |
| 2 | Unit tests verify socket serialization of components | met | `tests/test_notifications.py:449` — tests asserting `components` forwarded. |
| 3 | Producer review required on this child | unmet | Worklog metadata/comments indicate `needsProducerReview=true` for SA-0MM03Y5Y41KUITF7. |

### Scheduler Test Button Command (SA-0MM03YIY609CP27Y) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `test-button` CommandSpec auto-registered with 15m frequency | met | `ampa/scheduler.py:451-463` — `test-button` spec created with `frequency_minutes=15`. |
| 2 | Command calls `notifications.notify()` with correct message and two buttons | met | `ampa/scheduler.py:481-500` — `_send_test_button_message()` builds components and calls `notify()`. |
| 3 | Duplicate sends on restart / dedup logic | partial | `ampa/scheduler.py:562-586 & 706-725` — cleanup/wait logic exists but no unit/runtime proof of restart dedup was provided. |

### Documentation and Integration Test (SA-0MM03YXKC1YO8Q9V) — completed/in_review

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `ampa/README.md` contains Interactive Buttons section and examples | met | `ampa/README.md:443-486` — `## Interactive Buttons (MVP)` section with protocol and usage examples. |
| 2 | End-to-end integration test (notify -> socket -> View -> interaction -> ack) | partial | `tests/test_discord_bot.py:676-706` — socket->view unit tests exist; no mocked end‑to‑end test asserting `interaction.response.send_message()` was found. |

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: two verification gaps remain — (1) add an explicit unit/integration test that mocks `discord.Interaction` to exercise `on_interaction` and assert `interaction.response.send_message()` is called with the expected acknowledgement, and (2) provide a test or runtime proof that scheduler duplicate‑send/dedup behavior on restart is handled (or obtain producer sign‑off documenting expected behavior). Additionally, two child work items are flagged `needsProducerReview=true`.

# AMPA Audit Result

## Summary

The implementation in `ampa/discord_bot.py` largely satisfies the interactive button handler behaviour: the bot registers an `on_interaction` handler, constructs and sends the expected acknowledgement message, and attaches views for component payloads. However two acceptance criteria are not fully met: there are no unit tests that assert the acknowledgement text for interactions, and the code does not emit an explicit warning when a custom_id is unknown (it sends a generic ack but only logs informational messages for non-test ids). Because of these gaps the work item should remain open for follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | The bot handles `discord.Interaction` events for button clicks | met | ampa/discord_bot.py:235 — `@client.event` `on_interaction` registered and receives Interaction objects |
| 2 | The acknowledgement message format is: "You selected {label}, good luck. (clicked by {user}#{discriminator}, {ISO timestamp})" | met | ampa/discord_bot.py:261-267 — `label` derived from `custom_id` and `ack_message` composed exactly in the required format |
| 3 | The interaction is responded to within the 3-second Discord timeout (no deferred responses needed for MVP) | met | ampa/discord_bot.py:256-269 & ampa/discord_bot.py:126-144 — `_route_interaction` is synchronous/fast and code calls `interaction.response.send_message()` immediately |
| 4 | Unknown `custom_id` values are handled gracefully (log warning, send generic acknowledgement) | partial | ampa/discord_bot.py:261-267 & ampa/discord_bot.py:150-156 — code sends a generic "Unknown" label for empty ids and logs an info for non-test ids, but does not emit a dedicated warning when a custom_id cannot be resolved |
| 5 | Interactions for non-button component types (if any) are ignored gracefully | met | ampa/discord_bot.py:243-247 — handler checks `interaction.type != InteractionType.component` and returns after logging debug |
| 6 | Unit tests verify the correct acknowledgement format is produced for known and unknown custom_ids | unmet | tests/test_discord_bot.py:642-706 & tests/test_discord_bot.py:543-551 — tests cover socket protocol, component construction and `_route_interaction()` behavior, but there are no tests that simulate a `discord.Interaction` and assert the acknowledgement message sent via `interaction.response.send_message()` |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: 1 acceptance criterion is unmet (unit tests for acknowledgement format are missing) and 1 is partial (no explicit warning when a custom_id is unknown). Address these two items and rerun tests before closing.

      "description": "Extend the AMPA Discord bot with interactive button support: a new scheduler command sends a periodic \"Blue or Red?\" test message with `discord.ui.Button` components every 15 minutes; clicking a button produces an in-channel acknowledgement with clicker identity and timestamp, routed through the conversation_manager plumbing (no-op for MVP).

## Problem statement

The AMPA Discord bot (`ampa/discord_bot.py`) sends one-way plain-text notifications. There is no mechanism for Discord users to interact with bot messages. An MVP is needed to prove out the full round-trip: bot sends a message with clickable buttons, user clicks one, bot acknowledges the choice in-channel. This unblocks future interactive workflows (delegation approval, audit responses, operator confirmations).

## Users

- **Producers/operators** who want to verify that interactive Discord workflows are functional and that the bot can receive user input via buttons.
- **Any workspace member** in the channel: the MVP allows any user to click the buttons; the acknowledgement includes clicker identity and timestamp.

### Example user stories

- As a Producer, I want the bot to send a periodic test message with Blue and Red buttons so I can verify that interactive button flows are working end-to-end.
- As a team member, I want to click Blue or Red and see an immediate in-channel acknowledgement that includes who clicked and when.
- As a maintainer, I want a generic component protocol in the socket API so future interactive messages (delegation approval, audit responses) can be built without further protocol changes.

## Success criteria

- The bot sends a test message (\"Testing interactivity, Blue or Red?\") with two clickable `discord.ui.Button` components (labeled \"Blue\" and \"Red\") to the configured channel every 15 minutes, driven by a new scheduler command.
- When a user clicks a button, the bot replies in-channel with an acknowledgement: e.g. \"You selected Blue, good luck. (clicked by USERNAME#DISCRIMINATOR, 2026-02-24T12:00:00Z)\". No external persistence is required.
- The Unix socket protocol between `notifications.py` and `discord_bot.py` is extended with a generic `components` field that allows any caller to send messages with button components. The bot interprets this field and constructs `discord.ui.View`/`discord.ui.Button` objects.
- Button interaction handling plumbing routes through the existing `conversation_manager`/`responder` system, but for the MVP test message the conversation manager integration is wired as a no-op (acknowledge only; no session is started or resumed).
- Mock-based unit tests verify: (a) the extended socket protocol correctly handles component payloads, (b) button message construction produces valid `discord.ui.View`/`discord.ui.Button` objects, and (c) interaction callback handling produces the correct acknowledgement format.
- A short section in `ampa/README.md` documents how to enable the test message, required Discord bot permissions, and the component protocol.
- All existing tests continue to pass; no regressions in current notification delivery.

## Constraints

- Implementation must use **Python / discord.py** (the existing bot stack). No Node.js or discord.js.
- The bot currently uses `discord.Intents.default()`. Button interactions are delivered via the Gateway without MESSAGE_CONTENT intent, but the bot application must have Gateway-based interactions enabled in the Discord Developer Portal.
- The socket protocol extension must be backward-compatible: existing callers sending `{\"content\": \"...\"}` must continue to work unchanged.
- The scheduler command must respect Discord rate limits; the 15-minute interval is safe but the implementation should not allow duplicate scheduled sends if the scheduler restarts.
- No external persistence of button clicks is required for the MVP. The in-channel acknowledgement is sufficient.
- The `AMPA_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` env var (already configured) is used for the test message channel. No new channel configuration is needed.
- `discord.ui.View` objects have a default timeout of 180 seconds; the implementation must set an appropriate timeout (or `None`) so buttons remain clickable between scheduled sends.

## Existing state

- **`ampa/discord_bot.py`** (327 lines): `AMPABot` class with `discord.Client`, Unix socket server, `_send_to_discord()` sends plain text only via `channel.send(content)`. No `discord.ui.View`, `discord.ui.Button`, or `on_interaction` handler.
- **`ampa/notifications.py`** (316 lines): `notify()` function sends JSON over Unix socket. Protocol supports `{\"content\": \"...\"}` or `{\"title\": \"...\", \"body\": \"...\"}` — no component/button fields.
- **`ampa/conversation_manager.py`** (232 lines): `start_conversation()` / `resume_session()` API for sessions waiting for human input. Can serve as the backend for button click routing in future interactive workflows.
- **`ampa/responder.py`** (60 lines): Maps `action: accept|decline|respond` payloads to `conversation_manager.resume_session()`. Potential wire target for button interactions.
- **`ampa/scheduler.py`**: Bot supervision via `_ensure_bot_running()`, scheduler command framework. New commands can be added following the existing pattern.
- **`tests/test_discord_bot.py`** (464 lines): Uses `FakeChannel` mock and `asyncio.run()` pattern. Template for new button-related tests.
- **`tests/test_notifications.py`** (431 lines): Uses `_FakeSocketServer` for protocol testing. Template for component payload tests.
- The parent epic SA-0MLXEN5Q91FMXKEB explicitly deferred interactive buttons to v2+. This work item fulfills that deferred scope.

## Desired change

1. **Extend socket protocol**: Add an optional `components` field to the JSON protocol. When present, it describes button components the bot should attach to the message. Example payload:
   ```json
   {
     \"content\": \"Testing interactivity, Blue or Red?\",
     \"components\": [
       {
         \"type\": \"button\",
         \"label\": \"Blue\",
         \"style\": \"primary\",
         \"custom_id\": \"test_blue\"
       },
       {
         \"type\": \"button\",
         \"label\": \"Red\",
         \"style\": \"danger\",
         \"custom_id\": \"test_red\"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

2. **Extend `discord_bot.py`**: Update `_send_to_discord()` (or add a new method) to construct `discord.ui.View` with `discord.ui.Button` components when the payload includes `components`. Register an `on_interaction` handler that acknowledges button clicks with the clicker identity and timestamp. Wire the interaction handler to call through to the conversation_manager/responder system (no-op for the MVP test message).

3. **Extend `notifications.py`**: Update `notify()` to accept and forward a `components` parameter through the socket protocol.

4. **New scheduler command**: Add a scheduler command that sends the test button message every 15 minutes via `notifications.notify()`.

5. **Tests**: Add mock-based unit tests for component protocol handling, button construction, and interaction acknowledgement.

6. **Documentation**: Add a short section to `ampa/README.md` documenting how to enable the interactive test message, required Discord bot permissions, and how the component protocol works.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLXEN5Q91FMXKEB** — \"Implement Discord bot to replace webhook-based notifications\" (completed, parent epic): v1 notifications-only bot. This item is the first v2 interactive feature.
- **SA-0MLYL6GWK0ED513I** — \"Discord Bot Process Core\" (completed): defines the current bot architecture, socket protocol, and `_send_to_discord()`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Additional related work items

The interactive button test message scheduler command should follow the same pattern.

- **SA-0MLYL7F5H0E9D72U** — \"Scheduler Webhook Migration\" (completed): Migrated all ~14 scheduler webhook call sites to `notifications.notify()`. Establishes the calling conventions and test patterns for scheduler code that sends messages through the notification API — directly relevant since the new test-button scheduler command will also call `notifications.notify()`.

- **SA-0MLC7CT4T0KSMUTM** — \"Improve scheduler Discord message formatting\" (completed): Established Markdown formatting conventions for Discord messages sent by the scheduler. The interactive button test message content and acknowledgement format should follow these conventions.

- **SA-0MLXENM2Q08JOQI3** — \"Extract and consolidate webhook/notification logic from scheduler into ampa/notifications.py\" (open): This item concerns further refactoring of `notifications.py`. The interactive button work extends the same module's `notify()` function with a `components` parameter; implementers should be aware of potential merge conflicts or overlapping changes if both items are worked on concurrently.

### Repository artefacts

- **`ampa/discord_bot.py`** — Primary modification target. Currently defines `AMPABot` with `_send_to_discord(content: str)` which sends plain text only. The `components` protocol extension and `on_interaction` handler will be added here.

- **`ampa/notifications.py`** — Defines `notify()` at line 187. The function signature and socket serialization must be extended to accept and forward a `components` list.

- **`ampa/scheduler.py`** — Defines `CommandSpec` (line 104), `_ensure_bot_running()` (line 633), and the command framework. The new periodic test-button command will be registered as a `CommandSpec`.

- **`ampa/responder.py`** — Maps `action: accept|decline|respond` payloads to `conversation_manager.resume_session()`. Future interactive workflows will extend this mapping for button-driven actions.

- **`tests/test_discord_bot.py`** — Contains `FakeChannel` mock and existing `_send_to_discord` tests (lines 258-293). New button construction and interaction tests should follow these patterns.

- **`tests/test_notifications.py`** — Contains `_FakeSocketServer` for protocol testing. Component payload serialization tests should follow this pattern.

- **`tests/test_conversation_manager.py`** — Contains tests for `start_conversation` / `resume_session` flow, useful reference for verifying the no-op conversation_manager integration.

- **`ampa/README.md`** — Current documentation includes bot token setup and scheduler usage. The interactive button documentation section should be added here following established conventions.

- **`ampa/scheduler_schema.md`** — Documents the scheduler command schema including `metadata` fields. The new test-button command should be documented here.

### Key files

- `ampa/discord_bot.py` — primary modification target (bot process, socket handler, Discord send)
- `ampa/notifications.py` — socket client, `notify()` API extension
- `ampa/conversation_manager.py` — future integration point for button-driven session responses
- `ampa/responder.py` — future integration point for button action mapping
- `ampa/scheduler.py` — new scheduler command for periodic test message
- `tests/test_discord_bot.py` — test patterns to follow
- `tests/test_notifications.py` — protocol test patterns to follow

## Notes / resolved decisions

- **Language**: Python / discord.py (not discord.js as in the source intake WL-0MLZUAFTZ13LXA6X from another project).
- **Button click handling**: Plumbing routes through conversation_manager/responder, but for the MVP test message the conversation manager call is a no-op (acknowledge only in Discord).
- **Socket protocol**: Generic `components` field added to the protocol (not hardcoded message styles).
- **Scheduling**: New scheduler command, not inline in the scheduler loop.
- **Testing**: Mock-based unit tests following existing patterns (FakeChannel, asyncio.run()).
- **Schedule interval**: 15 minutes.
- **Persistence**: NOT required for MVP. The in-channel acknowledgement is sufficient.
- **Parent relationship**: Child of SA-0MLXEN5Q91FMXKEB (Discord bot epic, v2 interactive features).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Interaction timeout**: Discord requires interaction responses within 3 seconds or via deferred response. Mitigation: reply immediately to button interactions with the acknowledgement message; do not perform blocking work before responding.
- **View persistence across bot restarts**: `discord.ui.View` objects are in-memory; if the bot restarts, buttons on previously sent messages become unresponsive. Mitigation: acceptable for MVP (test messages are re-sent every 15 minutes). Document this limitation.
- **Protocol backward compatibility**: Adding `components` to the socket protocol could break callers that validate response shapes strictly. Mitigation: the field is optional and ignored when absent; existing payloads work unchanged. Add protocol version or capability negotiation as a future item if needed.
- **Scope creep**: Additional features (analytics dashboards, persistent click logs, role-restricted clicks, slash commands, embed-based responses) may be proposed during implementation. Mitigation: record extras as separate work items linked via `discovered-from:SA-0MM01V1HM0JA8XVL` and keep MVP narrowly scoped to the Blue/Red test message.
- **Discord Developer Portal configuration**: The bot application may need \"Message Content Intent\" or interaction endpoint configuration changes. Mitigation: button interactions do not require MESSAGE_CONTENT intent, but verify the bot has the interactions URL configured (or uses Gateway-based interactions, which discord.py handles automatically).

## Assumptions

- `AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and `AMPA_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` are already configured in the runtime environment (existing v1 bot setup).

data.comment:
## Root Cause Identified (SA-0MM1W49L40AO664Z investigation)

The bug has two contributing factors:

1. **Label accumulation on GitHub**: GH issue #52 has 3 conflicting stage labels (wl:stage:idea, wl:stage:in_review, wl:stage:done) because old stage labels are not removed when a new stage is applied. The wl:stage:in_review label was also re-added by rgardler-msft at 17:41 on Feb 25 after SorraTheOrc changed it to done at 03:14.

2. **Importer does not resolve conflicts**: When multiple wl:stage: labels exist, the importer does not pick the most recently added one. Since wl:stage:in_review is present and matches the local value, the importer considers the item unchanged.

### Required fixes (three separate concerns)
- **Fix 1 (wl github push)**: Remove old wl:stage: labels when pushing a new stage value
- **Fix 2 (wl github import)**: Handle multiple wl:stage: labels - either use event timeline to pick most recent, or warn about conflicts
- **Fix 3 (data cleanup)**: Remove stale labels from GH issue #52

See full investigation comment on SA-0MM1W49L40AO664Z.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
## Critical finding: Bug confirmed even with clean labels

After removing all stale/conflicting labels from GH issue #52 (leaving only wl:stage:done, wl:status:completed, wl:priority:medium, wl:tag:do-not-delegate), re-ran `wl github import`:

- Result: 0 items updated (351 scanned)
- The importer DID update `githubIssueUpdatedAt` to 2026-02-25T18:47:46Z (matching the GH issue)
- But it DID NOT update the stage from `in_review` to `done`

This proves the bug is NOT caused by conflicting labels alone. The importer's conflict resolution logic prefers the local stage value over the remote GitHub label, even when the GitHub label has clearly changed. The importer treats the local `updatedAt` as more authoritative.

The root cause is likely in the importer's merge/conflict resolution: when local and remote values differ, it appears to prefer local values for fields like stage, perhaps because the local `updatedAt` timestamp is more recent than the GitHub `updated_at`.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
## Investigation Results: Label-sync failure for GH issue #52

### Summary
Reproduced the bug. The importer ran successfully but did NOT update the local worklog item SA-0ML7OB0U70BVLHF7 (Dead-letter Final-failure Handling). The local stage remains `in_review` despite GitHub having a `wl:stage:done` label.

### Root Cause: Multiple conflicting stage labels on GitHub issue #52
GitHub issue #52 currently has **three** `wl:stage:` labels simultaneously:
- `wl:stage:idea` (added Feb 5, never removed)
- `wl:stage:in_review` (added Feb 21, removed Feb 25 03:14, **re-added Feb 25 17:41**)
- `wl:stage:done` (added Feb 25 03:14)

The full label set: `wl:priority:P2, wl:priority:medium, wl:stage:done, wl:stage:idea, wl:stage:in_review, wl:status:completed, wl:tag:do-not-delegate`

### Two distinct problems identified

**Problem 1 - Label hygiene (data issue):** When `wl github push` or manual label changes add a new stage label, the previous stage label(s) are NOT removed. This causes label accumulation. The `wl:stage:idea` label was added on Feb 5 and never cleaned up when later stages were applied.

**Problem 2 - Importer conflict resolution (code issue):** When the importer encounters multiple conflicting `wl:stage:` labels on a GitHub issue, it appears to either: (a) pick the one matching the existing local value and report no change, or (b) be unable to determine which label is authoritative and skip the update entirely. Either way, the import reports 0 updates.

### Evidence
- Before import: stage=in_review, status=completed
- Import result: {success: true, updated: 0, created: 0, totalIssues: 351}
- After import: stage=in_review, status=completed (UNCHANGED)
- GH label event timeline confirms wl:stage:in_review was re-added AFTER wl:stage:done
- Snapshots saved: /tmp/wl_issue52_before.json, /tmp/wl_issue52_after.json, /tmp/wl_github_import_repro2.log

### Recommended fixes
1. **wl github push**: When pushing a stage change, remove old wl:stage: labels before adding the new one (label replacement, not accumulation)
2. **wl github import**: When multiple wl:stage: labels exist, use the label event timeline to determine the most recently added one, or warn about conflicts
3. **Immediate data fix**: Clean up GH issue #52 by removing stale wl:stage:idea and wl:stage:in_review labels, keeping only wl:stage:done

data.comment:
Completed label cleanup on GH issue #52. Removed stale labels: wl:stage:idea, wl:stage:in_review, wl:priority:P2. Remaining labels are clean: wl:stage:done, wl:status:completed, wl:priority:medium, wl:tag:do-not-delegate.

However, re-running `wl github import` still did not update the local stage from in_review to done. The importer updated githubIssueUpdatedAt but not the stage field. This confirms the bug is in the importer's conflict resolution, not just in label accumulation.

Data cleanup is complete but the underlying import bug persists independently.

## Summary

The implementation provides a focused poller and a clear query/normalization pipeline (ampa/audit_poller.py) that is exercised by the poll-and-handoff orchestrator. However, the implementation uses `None` to signal query failures while the acceptance criteria require returning an empty list on failure — this mismatch means not all acceptance criteria are satisfied and the item should not be closed as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Queries `wl list --stage in_review --json` via the provided `run_shell` callable | met | ampa/audit_poller.py:151 — calls `run_shell("wl list --stage in_review --json", ...)`. |
| 2 | Handles JSON response as list, dict with `workItems`/`items`/`data` keys, or empty | met | ampa/audit_poller.py:180 — branches for `list` and dict keys ("workItems","work_items","items","data") and fallback key check. |
| 3 | Deduplicates candidates by work item ID | met | ampa/audit_poller.py:195 — builds `unique` dict keyed by id and returns unique values. |
| 4 | Returns an empty list on non-zero exit code or invalid JSON, logging the error | unmet | ampa/audit_poller.py:164 — logs warning and returns `None` on non-zero exit; ampa/audit_poller.py:173 — returns `None` on JSON parse failure. |
| 5 | When `wl list` returns a non-JSON string, the function returns an empty list and logs an error | unmet | ampa/audit_poller.py:172-176 — JSON parse exception is caught and `None` is returned (not an empty list). |
| 6 | Does not raise exceptions — returns empty list and logs errors | partial | ampa/audit_poller.py:150-162 — exceptions are caught and logged (no raise), but the function returns `None` on failure instead of an empty list as specified. |

## Children Status

No children.

## Recommendation

This item cannot be closed: 2 acceptance criteria expect an empty list on query failure but the implementation returns `None` (the poller treats `None` as a distinct "query_failed" outcome). Align the implementation with the acceptance criteria (or update the acceptance criteria to accept `None` / the poller-oriented contract). Possible resolutions: (1) change `_query_candidates` to return `[]` on failures (and let callers distinguish empty vs failure via logging/return-code), or (2) update the work item acceptance criteria to document `None` as the failure signal and keep the current poller behavior.

      "description": "# Intake Brief: Audit Detection & Polling Flow

> **Headline:** Extract audit candidate detection, cooldown filtering, and one-at-a-time selection from `TriageAuditRunner` into a focused polling module that queries for `in_review` items, applies store-based cooldown, and hands off the selected candidate to the descriptor-driven audit command handlers.

**Work Item:** SA-0MLYEOG9V107HE1D
**Parent:** SA-0MLWQI6DC09TF7IY (Audit integration & lifecycle updates)

## Problem Statement

The current `TriageAuditRunner` (~934 lines in `ampa/triage_audit.py`) combines candidate detection, cooldown filtering, audit skill invocation, result parsing, auto-completion, and state transitions into a single monolithic class. The sibling work item SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV extracts the audit command handlers. This item extracts the upstream detection and polling layer: querying for audit-ready items, filtering by cooldown, selecting the next candidate, and handing it off to the audit command handlers. This separation enables the detection logic to be tested and modified independently from audit execution.

## Users

- **AMPA scheduler (system):** Needs a clean polling interface to replace the candidate-detection portion of `TriageAuditRunner`, invoked via the scheduler's existing command routing (`wl-triage-audit` command).
  - *User story:* As the scheduler, I need the triage-audit command to detect audit-ready items and hand them to the audit command handlers, so that detection/cooldown logic is decoupled from audit execution and both can evolve independently.

- **Producer (human):** Benefits indirectly — work items in `in_review` are automatically picked up for audit without manual intervention, with cooldown intervals preventing redundant audits.
  - *User story:* As a producer, I want items that agents mark as `in_review` to be automatically detected and audited on a configurable interval, so that completed work is verified without me manually triggering audits.

## Success Criteria

1. A new module (e.g. `ampa/audit_poller.py` or similar) queries `wl list --stage in_review --json` to detect audit candidates, replacing the detection logic currently in `TriageAuditRunner`.
2. Per-item cooldown filtering uses only the persisted scheduler store (`last_audit_at_by_item`), removing the current comment-scanning approach (`wl comment list` per candidate).
3. The cooldown interval is sourced from the existing `audit_cooldown_hours` metadata in the scheduler store (default: 6 hours).
4. One candidate is selected per invocation cycle, sorted by `updated_at` ascending (oldest item first), matching the current behavior.
5. The `last_audit_at` timestamp for the selected item is persisted to the store immediately at handoff (before audit execution begins), preventing re-selection during long-running audits.
6. The selected candidate is handed off to the descriptor-driven audit command handlers (SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV) — this module does not invoke `opencode run \"/audit {id}\"` or process audit results itself.
7. The module is invoked via the scheduler's existing command routing, replacing `TriageAuditRunner.run()` as the handler for the `wl-triage-audit` command in `Scheduler.start_command()`.
8. When no candidates pass cooldown filtering, the module returns a \"no candidates\" result without error.
9. If the `wl list` query fails (non-zero exit, invalid JSON), the module logs the error and returns a structured error result without crashing the scheduler loop.
10. Unit tests cover: no items in `in_review`, all items within cooldown, mixed cooldown (some eligible, some not), oldest-first sorting, store persistence on handoff, query failure handling, and scheduler routing integration.

## Constraints

- **Detection scope is `in_review` only.** The parent work item mentions polling for `in_progress` and `blocked` items, but at this time only `in_review` items are candidates for audit. Expansion to other states can be a separate work item if needed.
- **No comment scanning.** Cooldown is determined solely from the persisted `last_audit_at_by_item` store, not from scanning comments. This simplifies the implementation and removes per-candidate `wl comment list` calls.
- **Handoff only.** This module selects candidates but does not invoke the audit skill or process results. It depends on SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV (audit command handlers) for audit execution.
- **One item per cycle.** Batch processing is out of scope. The module selects and hands off a single candidate per invocation.
- **Scheduler command routing preserved.** The module is invoked through the scheduler's `start_command()` mechanism for the `wl-triage-audit` command, not as an independent process.
- **No new external dependencies.** Python 3.10+, existing project dependencies only.

## Existing State

### Code
- `ampa/triage_audit.py` — `TriageAuditRunner` (~934 lines): monolithic class combining detection (`wl list --stage in_review`), dual-source cooldown (comment-based + store), candidate sorting, audit invocation, result parsing, auto-completion, Discord notifications, and state persistence.
- `ampa/scheduler.py` — `Scheduler.start_command()` (lines ~1192-1209): routes the `wl-triage-audit` command to `TriageAuditRunner.run()`.
- Scheduler store (`.worklog/ampa/scheduler_store.json`): persists `last_audit_at_by_item` dict under the triage-audit command's state key, mapping work item IDs to ISO timestamps.

### Detection flow (current)
1. Query: `wl list --stage in_review --json`
2. Normalize response (handle list/dict formats, deduplicate by ID)
3. For each candidate: check cooldown via comment scanning (`wl comment list`) AND store lookup
4. Filter items within cooldown
5. Sort remaining by `updated_at` ascending
6. Select first (oldest) item
7. Invoke audit skill, parse results, apply state transitions (all interleaved)

### Configuration
- `audit_cooldown_hours`: metadata field in command spec (default: 6 hours)
- `audit_cooldown_hours_in_review`: per-status override (no longer needed with in_review-only scope)

## Desired Change

Extract the detection and polling layer from `TriageAuditRunner` into a focused module:

1. **Candidate query:** Query `wl list --stage in_review --json` and normalize the response (handle list/dict JSON formats, deduplicate by ID).

2. **Cooldown filtering:** For each candidate, look up `last_audit_at_by_item[item_id]` from the scheduler store. If `(now - last_audit_at) < cooldown_hours`, skip the item. Items with no store entry are always eligible.

3. **Candidate selection:** Sort eligible items by `updated_at` ascending (oldest first, items with no timestamp sorted first). Select the first item.

4. **Store persistence on handoff:** Before handing off to the audit command handlers, write `last_audit_at_by_item[selected_id] = now` to the scheduler store. This prevents the same item from being re-selected if the audit takes longer than the polling interval.

5. **Handoff to handlers:** Pass the selected candidate to the audit command handlers (SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV). The handoff interface should be defined to accept a work item dict (as returned by `wl list`).

6. **Scheduler integration:** Update `Scheduler.start_command()` to route `wl-triage-audit` to this new module instead of `TriageAuditRunner.run()`.

7. **No-candidate result:** When no items pass cooldown checks, return a structured result indicating \"no candidates\" without raising an error.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep:** Expanding detection to other states (`in_progress`, `blocked`) or adding batch processing could grow this item. *Mitigation:* Record expansion as separate work items linked to SA-0MLYEOG9V107HE1D rather than expanding this item's scope.
- **Handoff interface mismatch:** The interface between this module and the audit command handlers (SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV) must be agreed before implementation. If the handlers expect a different input shape than what this module produces, integration will fail. *Mitigation:* Coordinate the handoff interface with SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV during planning.
- **Store-only cooldown loses comment-based recovery:** Removing comment-based cooldown detection means that if the store is lost or reset, all items become immediately eligible for re-audit. *Mitigation:* Accept this trade-off — the store is the authoritative source. Document that store loss triggers a re-audit cycle. Re-auditing is not harmful, only redundant.
- **Timing race on handoff persistence:** Writing `last_audit_at` before audit execution means that if the handler fails immediately, the item won't be re-selected until the cooldown expires. *Mitigation:* The handler should report failure back, allowing the poller to clear the timestamp if needed. Alternatively, accept the cooldown delay as a safeguard against retry storms.
- **`wl list` output format change:** If the `wl list --stage in_review --json` output format changes (e.g. key names, nesting), candidate normalization will break silently. *Mitigation:* Unit tests should validate against representative `wl list` output; normalization logic should fail explicitly on unrecognized formats.

### Assumptions

- The `wl list --stage in_review --json` command output format is stable.
- The scheduler store's `last_audit_at_by_item` dict structure is preserved.
- The `audit_cooldown_hours` metadata field is the sole source of cooldown interval configuration.
- The audit command handlers (SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV) will expose a callable interface that accepts a work item dict.
- The scheduler's command routing mechanism (`start_command()`) remains the integration point.
- One-item-per-cycle throughput is sufficient for the expected volume of `in_review` items.

# AMPA Audit Result

---
## Goal

Update the triage-audit tests and documentation to reflect the extracted detection/polling module (audit_poller) and the store-only cooldown model, and ensure the poller + handler integration implements the intended behavior (query -> cooldown -> oldest-first selection -> persist-before-handoff -> handler) with test coverage and docs aligned.

## Instructions

- Preserve the store-only cooldown model (no comment-scanning). The scheduler store holds last_audit_at_by_item and cooldown is enforced by comparing now - last_audit_at to audit_cooldown_hours.
- Poller responsibilities:
  - Query the worklog for candidates (wl list --stage ... --json).
  - Normalize and deduplicate responses.
  - Apply the store-based cooldown filter.
  - Sort eligible candidates by updated_at ascending (items with no timestamp first).
  - Persist last_audit_at for the selected item to the scheduler store BEFORE calling the handler.
  - Hand off the selected candidate to a handler implementing the handoff protocol; the poller must not itself run the audit command (opencode run "/audit <id>").
- Handoff protocol intent: the work item asked for a Protocol that accepts a work item dict and returns a structured result (PollerResult). Currently the code documents/uses a callable that returns bool; reconcile this type/semantic mismatch with the spec.
- Do not introduce new external dependencies.
- Tests should mock run_shell, the store, and handler behavior; cover edge cases: no items, all within cooldown, mixed cooldown, oldest-first selection, persist-before-handoff, query failure handling, handler exception behavior, and shell/run invocation kwargs (e.g., shell=True).
- Documentation should reflect actual runtime choices (stage queried, env var names). If there are naming decisions (AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN vs AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK), either update docs or clarify intent with stakeholders.

## Discoveries

- New module implemented: ampa/audit_poller.py. It contains:
  - PollerOutcome enum (no_candidates, handed_off, query_failed)
  - PollerResult dataclass (outcome, selected_item_id, error)
  - AuditHandoffHandler Protocol (runtime_checkable) declared, but its __call__ is annotated to return bool (docstring earlier asked for a structured result — mismatch).
  - _query_candidates(...) implemented; it invokes run_shell with "wl list --stage in_progress --json" and returns None on failures (non-zero exit / invalid JSON / execution error) rather than an empty list — tests and current poll_and_handoff use None to indicate query_failed.
  - _filter_by_cooldown(), _select_candidate(), _item_updated_ts(), and the orchestrator poll_and_handoff() — which persists last_audit_at before calling the handler and returns PollerResult outcomes.
- Tests/test_audit_poller.py present and comprehensive: runtime protocol checks, many query shape cases, cooldown and selection tests, and poll_and_handoff full-flow tests (including persist-before-handoff, query failure -> query_failed, handler exception -> handed_off).
- docs/triage-audit.md updated to describe detection vs. execution separation and structured audit output. The doc refers to querying "in_review" items and documents AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN (bot-token model). There is an env-var naming mismatch in some acceptance text (work item asked for AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK while repo/docs use AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN).
- Work items and audit comments: SA-0MM2FF1WW1FVP8H7 ("Update tests and documentation") is marked completed / in_review in the worklog with multiple AMPA audit comments indicating acceptance criteria were met. The audit work chain shows the poller extraction and related tasks completed and integrated with scheduler routing.
- Behavioral mismatches flagged in earlier audits (and partially addressed):
  - Protocol return type vs acceptance text (bool vs PollerResult).
  - _query_candidates return value on failure (None vs empty list originally requested). Current tests expect None and poll_and_handoff maps None -> query_failed; some ACs asked for returning [] on failure — this is a spec/implementation divergence to decide on.
  - Stage name usage: docs often say `in_review` but ampa/audit_poller.py currently calls "wl list --stage in_progress --json". Confirm which stage should be queried (in_review vs in_progress) and align code, tests, and docs accordingly.
- Scheduler wiring and tests were updated across the repo: scheduler routing now invokes poll_and_handoff in the scheduler flow (worklog comments show integration). Some local branches and uncommitted edits exist in the workspace referenced by the audits.

## Accomplished

- Implemented ampa/audit_poller.py with full pipeline:
  - Query normalization and deduplication
  - Store-based cooldown filter
  - Oldest-first selection logic
  - Persist-before-handoff semantics
  - PollerResult/enum types and documented AuditHandoffHandler protocol
- Added/updated tests in tests/test_audit_poller.py to cover:
  - Query shapes, shell kwargs, failure behavior
  - Cooldown filtering edge cases and timestamps parsing (Z suffix, invalid ISO)
  - Candidate selection ordering and tie cases
  - poll_and_handoff orchestrator flows (handed_off, no_candidates, query_failed, persist order, handler exceptions)
- Updated documentation: docs/triage-audit.md describes the detection/hand-off/extraction flow and structured audit output. It documents the bot-token model and the store-first cooldown model.
- Integrated poller into scheduler routing (worklog shows scheduler wiring updated and tests updated accordingly).
- Updated tests/test_triage_audit.py and other test suites were adapted to new routing in the repo (worklog and comments note many behavioral tests passing); some tests and local commits were referenced in the audit comments.

Work still in progress / open decisions:
- Decide and align the AuditHandoffHandler return type/contract: return bool (current) or structured PollerResult / other structured type as originally requested. Update Protocol, handler implementations, and tests accordingly.
- Decide and align _query_candidates failure semantics: return None to signal query failure (as implemented) or return [] and treat other signals differently. Update docs/ACs/tests to match decision.
- Confirm the stage used in wl query (in_review vs in_progress) and align code/tests/docs. Several audit comments flagged inconsistent usage.
- Resolve docs env-var naming mismatch (AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN vs AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK) — either update docs/ACs or add fallback behavior.
- Finish any outstanding test refactors in integration-level triage tests (if any remain), and run the full test suite to ensure no regressions.

## Relevant files / directories

Files we inspected and that are directly relevant to continuing the work:

- Implementation
  - ampa/audit_poller.py — the new poller module (query, normalization, cooldown filter, selection, persistence, handoff, PollerResult, PollerOutcome, AuditHandoffHandler)
  - ampa/triage_audit.py — execution/handler module (audit execution, structured-report extraction, Discord, comment posting). (Referenced in docs/tests; used as handler)
  - ampa/scheduler.py — scheduler routing and wiring to poller/handler (integration point)

- Tests
  - tests/test_audit_poller.py — unit tests for poller protocol, query shapes, cooldown, selection, and poll_and_handoff orchestrator (read and exercised)
  - tests/test_triage_audit.py — integration/behavior tests for the audit flow (referenced heavily in worklog; may have been updated to new routing)
  - tests/* — other tests referencing triage/audit flows (used in worklog reports)

- Documentation
  - docs/triage-audit.md — documentation of detection, handoff, structured output, configuration, and migration notes (bot-token vs webhook)
  - skill/audit/SKILL.md — referenced for the /audit command output format (structured delimiters)

- Worklog / audit evidence
  - .worklog/worklog-data.jsonl — worklog JSON that contains many AMPA audit comments, task wiring, and status/acceptance evidence (useful for context & acceptance history)
  - ampa/scheduler_store.json / ampa/scheduler_store_example.json — scheduler store/example used for persisted last_audit_at_by_item and configured metadata (cooldown_hours, etc.)

- Misc (tests and CI)
  - pyproject.toml / test config — testing environment (pytest plugins and versions referenced in test output)
  - local branches / uncommitted edits (mentioned in worklog comments) — be aware there may be local workspace changes when running tests.

## Suggested next steps for the next agent

1. Verify and reconcile protocol contract:
   - Decide whether AuditHandoffHandler should return bool (current implementation) or a structured result (PollerResult). If changing, update ampa/audit_poller.py Protocol, any handler adapters, and tests/test_audit_poller.py (runtime Protocol checks).
2. Decide failure signaling for _query_candidates:
   - If you accept current behavior (None -> query_failed), update any acceptance text and docs to match. Otherwise, change _query_candidates to return [] on failure and adjust poll_and_handoff and tests.
3. Confirm which stage to query:
   - Inspect scheduler/requirements and decide whether to query "in_review" or "in_progress". Update ampa/audit_poller.py command string, docs/triage-audit.md, and tests accordingly.
4. Run the test suite (targeted to the poller and triage tests):
   - Run pytest tests/test_audit_poller.py and tests/test_triage_audit.py locally; fix any mismatches or failing assertions (shell kwargs, stage strings, return conventions).
5. Address doc/env-var mismatch:
   - Choose which env var naming is canonical (AMPA_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN vs AMPA_DISCORD_WEBHOOK), update docs and tests, and add a migration note or fallback behavior in notifications module.
6. Re-run integration checks and ensure scheduler routing still calls poll_and_handoff with an appropriate handler adapter that calls TriageAuditRunner.run() with work_item kwarg.
7. If changes are made, update work item SA-0MM2FF1WW1FVP8H7 comments or create a short worklog entry documenting the clarifications and code changes for producer review.

If you want me (or the next agent) to continue:
- I can apply one specific decision (e.g., change Protocol to return PollerResult) and edit ampa/audit_poller.py + tests accordingly, run tests, and open a PR; or
- I can run the test suites locally and report failures with exact stack traces and failing assertions so we can prioritize fixes.

# AMPA Audit Result

---
## Goal

Implement descriptor-driven audit command handlers (audit_result, audit_fail, close_with_audit) that validate from-state, evaluate pre/post invariants via the engine's InvariantEvaluator, perform state transitions according to the workflow descriptor, return structured audit results, and include unit tests. The broader aim is to replace the legacy/monolithic triage-audit runner with descriptor-driven handlers while preserving audit polling, cooldown, evidence capture, auto-completion heuristics, and Discord notifications.

## Instructions

- Implement three new descriptor-driven handlers for the audit commands that:
  - Confirm the work item is in a valid from-state (using the workflow descriptor).
  - Evaluate pre-invariants before applying transitions (using InvariantEvaluator or engine-provided APIs).
  - Apply the transition if pre-invariants pass and perform any side-effects (wl update, wl comment add, notification).
  - Return a structured result indicating success/failure and reasons (machine-friendly).
  - Evaluate post-invariants where appropriate (or ensure post-invariant checks are performed by the engine / callback paths).
- Preserve independent audit flow behavior:
  - Audit flow detects audit-ready items (in_review, in_progress, blocked) via the existing audit poller (ampa/audit_poller.py).
  - The audit flow must not depend on engine lifecycle hooks; it operates by polling and handoff.
- Rewire scheduler routing:
  - Replace the TriageAuditRunner / opencode-run-based invocation path with a dispatcher that routes pre-selected candidates (from the poller) to the descriptor-driven handlers.
  - Persist last_audit_at before handoff (poller already does this).
- Tests and verification:
  - Add unit tests for each handler covering happy path, pre-invariant failure, wrong-from-state rejection, audit-fail behavior, and close_with_audit conditions (PR merged + no open children).
  - Refactor tests/test_triage_audit.py (or create new tests/test_audit_handlers.py) to mock wl/opencode/gh as needed.
- Backward compatibility / cleanup:
  - Keep TriageAuditRunner as a compatibility shim only while handlers are developed, then remove or drastically reduce it per cleanup task.
  - Preserve existing structured `# AMPA Audit Result` comments format unless replaced by a documented structured output contract.
- Constraints to respect:
  - Do not add new external dependencies.
  - Audit skill (skill/audit/SKILL.md) is consumed as-is; handlers should expect the skill output format until a new structured contract is agreed and implemented.
  - The audit flow must maintain per-status cooldown behavior (metadata-driven audit_cooldown_hours).
  - The audit flow must preserve Discord/webhook notification behavior (notifications_module).

## Discoveries

- Existing extraction/refactors already completed and present in repo:
  - The triage-audit logic was extracted from the monolithic scheduler into ampa/triage_audit.py (TriageAuditRunner).
  - Candidate detection/cooldown/selection was extracted into ampa/audit_poller.py; the poller persists last_audit_at_by_item and hands off a single selected candidate to a handler.
- The current runtime path:
  - Scheduler.start_command() routes the "wl-triage-audit" command through the poller which then hands off to TriageAuditRunner.
  - TriageAuditRunner currently invokes the audit skill via opencode run "/audit {id}" and posts structured `# AMPA Audit Result` comments, sends notifications, and performs auto-completion heuristics.
- Gaps / mismatches observed:
  - Multiple audit outputs and automated audits indicate the descriptor-driven handlers and invariant-based evaluation are still unmet in the codebase (code still relies on TriageAuditRunner/opencode-run).
  - Work items show a mix of statuses: SA-0MM5M39OA01I7I1D (implement descriptor-driven handlers) is marked completed/in_review in WL metadata, but static code review and AMPA audit reports indicate the handlers were not implemented as descriptor-driven handlers (legacy runner still used). There is a timestamp/merge conflict recorded for this work item (sync log).
  - The poller implementation and store-backed cooldown are implemented and tested (ampa/audit_poller.py, tests/test_audit_poller.py).
  - Auto-completion heuristics exist (PR merged check via gh, children open check) and structured comments are produced; minor behavioral differences were observed in audit reports (e.g., whether needs-producer-review is reliably set).
- Important repo artifacts and specifications exist and must be consumed:
  - docs/workflow/workflow.yaml — canonical workflow descriptor defining commands (audit_result, audit_fail, close_with_audit) and invariants.
  - docs/workflow/workflow-schema.json — descriptor JSON Schema.
  - docs/workflow/engine-prd.md — engine PRD and command execution lifecycle (note: audit is out-of-scope for engine lifecycle hooks; audit flow must operate independently).
  - skill/audit/SKILL.md — current audit skill contract (markdown output with # Summary section).
- Tests and test scaffolding:
  - tests/test_triage_audit.py exists and was refactored/used previously. There are tests for poller/runner behavior and unit tests for cooldown and selection.
  - Many tests and automated audit comments reference the need to mock wl/opencode/gh and verify PR/child checks.

## Accomplished

- Extracted and modularized triage-audit logic:
  - ampa/triage_audit.py (TriageAuditRunner) was created to encapsulate audit execution logic.
  - ampa/audit_poller.py created to handle query → cooldown → selection → persist-before-handoff handoff.
  - Scheduler updated to route triage-audit through the new poller/handoff path.
- Implemented store-backed cooldown filtering and oldest-first candidate selection; tests for poller behaviors exist and pass.
- TriageAuditRunner currently executes audits by invoking the existing audit skill (opencode run "/audit {id}"), posts structured comments, sends notifications, and performs auto-completion when conditions are met.
- Several supporting work items and tasks completed (poller, cooldown, selection, scheduler routing, some test refactors). There are many audit comments and logs confirming the above changes were merged/committed in the repository history.
- Not yet completed (or evidence suggests not implemented in code):
  - Replacing TriageAuditRunner with descriptor-driven audit command handlers that use the workflow descriptor and InvariantEvaluator (audit_result, audit_fail, close_with_audit).
  - Full integration tests and unit tests for descriptor-driven handlers and invariant evaluation; test suite updates to assert descriptor-driven behavior.
  - Final cleanup/deprecation of TriageAuditRunner and removal of legacy marker-based parsing if replaced by structured output.

## What remains / Next steps

1. Implement descriptor-driven audit handlers:
   - New module (e.g., ampa/audit_handlers.py) that implements audit_result, audit_fail, close_with_audit handlers reading docs/workflow/workflow.yaml and using the engine's InvariantEvaluator or equivalent APIs.
   - Handlers should accept a pre-selected work_item dict (from the poller) and a run_shell / store / engine dependency so they can perform wl updates, comments, and notifications.
2. Integrate handlers into pipeline:
   - Update ampa/scheduler.py handoff/handler to call descriptor-driven handlers (instead of TriageAuditRunner.run).

3. Tests:
   - Add unit tests for each handler (happy path, pre-invariant failure, wrong from-state rejection, audit-failure recording).
   - Update/refactor tests/test_triage_audit.py to reference new handlers or add tests/test_audit_handlers.py.
   - Mock wl/opencode/gh/notifications in tests; assert structured result schemas are returned and posted comments follow the expected format.
4. Behavioral parity checks:
   - Verify auto-complete conditions: audit recommends closure, PR merged (gh pr view), no open children → apply wl update status=completed, stage=in_review, needs-producer-review=true (ensure the flag is set properly).
   - Ensure `# AMPA Audit Result` comment formatting or a new structured comment contract is produced and persisted.
5. Cleanup:
   - After handlers are implemented and tested, reduce or remove TriageAuditRunner (leave a compatibility shim if needed); remove or update legacy parsing logic if the audit skill output format is changed to structured output.
6. Synchronization/merge issues:
   - Resolve the noted metadata/timestamp conflict for SA-0MM5M39OA01I7I1D and confirm the work item state and repository reflect the new code.
7. Verification:
   - Run the relevant tests: pytest tests/test_audit_poller.py, tests/test_triage_audit.py (updated), new handler tests.
   - Execute an end-to-end run: start scheduler (or simulate poller handoff) with mocked run_shell and verify handlers run and post WL comments + notifications.

## Relevant files / directories (read, referenced, or that should be modified)

- Code and runtime glue:
  - ampa/scheduler.py — scheduler main; currently routes triage-audit through poller and hands off to TriageAuditRunner (needs update to call descriptor-driven handlers).
  - ampa/triage_audit.py — TriageAuditRunner (existing runner that invokes opencode run "/audit {id}"; to be replaced or shrunk).
  - ampa/audit_poller.py — poller: queries candidates, filters by store-backed cooldown, selects oldest, persists last_audit_at, hands off to handler.
  - ampa/delegation.py — delegation orchestrator (for context; ensure no delegation is reintroduced into audit flow).
  - ampa/scheduler_store.json and SchedulerStore — store persistence for last_audit_at_by_item.
  - ampa/scheduler_helpers.py, ampa/notifications.py — notification helpers used by audit flow.
  - ampa/engine/* — Engine and InvariantEvaluator types used by handlers (engine/core, engine/candidates). Handlers should use engine-provided InvariantEvaluator or an injected evaluator.
- Tests:
  - tests/test_triage_audit.py — existing triage/audit tests (needs refactor to new handlers or replacement).
  - tests/test_audit_poller.py — tests for the poller (present and passing).
  - tests/* (engine integration tests) — there are tests referencing audit_result command behavior (e.g., tests/test_engine_integration.py).
- Specs and documentation:
  - docs/workflow/workflow.yaml (and docs/workflow/workflow.json) — canonical workflow descriptor; defines audit_result, audit_fail, close_with_audit, pre/post invariants, roles.
  - docs/workflow/workflow-schema.json — descriptor schema to validate descriptor usage.
  - docs/workflow/engine-prd.md — engine PRD and execution lifecycle notes (audit flow is independent from engine lifecycle).
  - skill/audit/SKILL.md — audit skill contract (current prompt and expected markdown output).
- Other helpful artifacts:
  - .worklog/ and logs/ — worklog and automated audit reports give context and historical comments confirming refactors and test results.
  - tests mocking utilities or run_shell test doubles used by poller/runner tests.

> **Headline:** Refactor the AMPA scheduler's hard-coded triage audit logic into descriptor-driven audit command handlers that invoke the audit skill on work item completion, interpret results, and perform workflow-state lifecycle transitions.

**Work Item:** SA-0MLWQI6DC09TF7IY
**Parent:** SA-0MLPYRLRY0ODG6YH (AMPA unidirectional delegation, audit, and lifecycle management)

## Problem Statement

The AMPA scheduler's `_run_triage_audit()` method (~955 lines in `ampa/scheduler.py`) implements audit invocation, result parsing, auto-completion, and Discord notifications as monolithic hard-coded logic. The workflow descriptor (`docs/workflow/workflow.yaml`) defines three formal audit commands (`audit_result`, `audit_fail`, `close_with_audit`) with pre/post invariants and actor roles, but these are not consumed by the current code. This work item refactors the existing audit logic to be driven by the workflow descriptor, operating as an independent audit flow that detects items ready for audit and executes audit commands as part of the formal command execution lifecycle.

## Users

- **Producer (human):** Wants audit results to drive predictable, auditable lifecycle transitions so that work items reaching `in_review` have verified evidence of acceptance criteria being met.
  - *User story:* As a producer, I want audit results to automatically update work item lifecycle state with structured evidence, so that I can trust items marked `in_review` have passed quality verification.

- **AMPA scheduler (system):** Needs a descriptor-driven audit handler to replace its hard-coded `_run_triage_audit()`, so that audit behavior can be modified through workflow descriptor changes rather than code changes.
  - *User story:* As the scheduler, I need the audit flow to independently detect items ready for audit (e.g. items in `in_review` stage set by delegated agents) and invoke the audit skill, receiving structured results that drive the correct workflow-state transitions.

- **Delegated agent (AI):** Benefits indirectly — when an agent completes work and sets stage to `in_review`, the audit flow detects this and audits automatically without manual intervention.
  - *User story:* As a delegated agent, I want my completed work to be audited automatically so that successful implementations proceed to review without delays.

## Success Criteria

1. The three audit workflow commands (`audit_result`, `audit_fail`, `close_with_audit`) are implemented as descriptor-driven command handlers, consuming the workflow descriptor's states, invariants, and actor roles.
2. Audit is triggered via two mechanisms: (a) the audit flow independently polls for items in audit-ready states (e.g. `in_review` stage set by delegated agents on completion), and (b) periodically by the scheduler on a cooldown/polling basis for in-progress and in-review items. The audit flow does NOT depend on engine lifecycle hooks — it operates independently.
3. When audit recommends closure AND no open children exist AND the PR is merged, the system auto-completes the item: `status=completed`, `stage=in_review`, `needs-producer-review=true`.
4. When audit does not recommend closure, the system records gaps in a structured `wl comment` and leaves the work item open with the audit failure documented.
5. Audit results are captured as structured `wl comment` entries on the work item with headings (`# AMPA Audit Result`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Summary`).
6. Per-status cooldown logic is preserved: configurable intervals for `in_review`, `in_progress`, and `blocked` items, preventing redundant audits.
7. Discord webhook notifications are preserved: audit summary and completion announcements are sent to configured channels.
8. Pre/post invariants from the workflow descriptor (`requires_audit_result`, `audit_recommends_closure`, `audit_does_not_recommend_closure`) are evaluated as part of command execution.
9. Existing tests in `tests/test_triage_audit.py` are refactored to match the new descriptor-driven API, with `wl` and `opencode run` calls mocked.
10. The refactored audit integration operates independently from the engine core — it detects items in audit-ready states and processes them without requiring engine dispatch interfaces or lifecycle hooks.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by SA-0MLWQI60Q0CJGFO2 (engine core):** This work item depends on the engine core's descriptor loading and invariant evaluation being implemented. However, it does NOT depend on engine lifecycle hooks — the audit flow operates independently by polling for items in audit-ready states.
- **Refactor, not rewrite:** The existing `_run_triage_audit()` logic is refactored to use descriptor-driven command execution, not rewritten from scratch. Behavioral continuity with the current system is expected.
- **Audit skill is unchanged:** The audit skill (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`) is invoked as-is via `opencode run \"/audit {id}\"`. This work item does not modify the audit skill itself.
- **No new external dependencies:** Python 3.10+, using existing project dependencies.
- **Context assembly out of scope:** Building delegation payloads from codebase context is the engine core's responsibility. This work item consumes work item state to determine audit readiness.
- **Adjacent commands out of scope:** The workflow descriptor also defines `retry_delegation` (audit_failed -> delegated) and `escalate` (audit_failed -> escalated). These are downstream of `audit_fail` but are not part of this work item's scope. They may be implemented as part of engine core or a separate work item.

## Existing State

### Code
- `ampa/scheduler.py`, `_run_triage_audit()` (lines ~1366-2321): Current audit implementation including:
  - `wl in_progress` / `wl blocked` item listing
  - Per-item cooldown with configurable intervals per status
  - Audit skill invocation via `opencode run \"/audit {id}\"`
  - Output parsing: extracts `# Summary` section from audit output
  - Discord webhook: posts audit summary and completion notifications
  - `wl comment add` with `# AMPA Audit Result` heading
  - Auto-completion: checks PR merged (via `gh pr view`), no open children, audit recommends closure
  - State persistence: `last_audit_at_by_item` in scheduler store

### Specifications
- `docs/workflow/workflow.yaml`: Audit commands defined:
  - `audit_result`: from `in_review` to `audit_passed`, actor `QA`, pre-invariant `requires_audit_result`, post-invariant `audit_recommends_closure`
  - `audit_fail`: from `in_review` to `audit_failed`, actor `QA`, pre-invariant `requires_audit_result`, post-invariant `audit_does_not_recommend_closure`
  - `close_with_audit`: from `audit_passed` to `completed`/`in_review`, actor `PM`
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md`: Engine PRD defines the command execution lifecycle. Audit-specific sections (5.4, 5.5) have been removed from the engine PRD as audit is out of scope for the engine. The audit flow is referenced in the engine PRD's scope section and command table as belonging to this work item.
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md`: Audit failure scenario with retry

### Tests
- `tests/test_triage_audit.py`: Covers audit execution, auto-completion, cooldown, blocked items, audit-only mode, delegation from triage

## Desired Change

Refactor the AMPA scheduler's audit internals into descriptor-driven command handlers that operate as an independent audit flow:

1. **Audit command handlers:** Implement `audit_result`, `audit_fail`, and `close_with_audit` as handlers that follow the command execution lifecycle (confirm from-state, evaluate pre-invariants, apply state transition, execute command logic).

2. **Independent audit detection:** The audit flow independently polls for items in audit-ready states (e.g. items where a delegated agent has set stage to `in_review`). It does NOT rely on engine lifecycle hooks or post-dispatch callbacks. This decouples the audit flow from the engine core.

3. **Scheduled audit polling:** Preserve the scheduler's periodic audit polling for items that have been in `in_progress`, `in_review`, or `blocked` state longer than the configured cooldown interval. This complements the audit-ready detection.

4. **Auto-completion logic:** When `audit_result` succeeds (audit recommends closure), evaluate additional conditions (PR merged, no open children) and execute `close_with_audit` to transition to `completed`/`in_review` with `needs-producer-review=true`.

5. **Evidence capture:** Write structured `wl comment` entries with audit results, preserving the `# AMPA Audit Result` heading format. Include acceptance criteria evaluation, summary, and closure recommendation.

6. **Discord integration:** Preserve audit summary and completion notification webhooks, adapted to use the engine's observability/recording mechanism.

7. **Cooldown preservation:** Maintain per-status cooldown intervals (`in_review`, `in_progress`, `blocked`) from the existing implementation, stored in the scheduler state.

8. **Test refactoring:** Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to test the new descriptor-driven API. Mock external calls (`wl`, `opencode run`, `gh pr view`). Ensure behavioral parity with existing tests.

Evidence-driven review of the find-related skill (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9), re-measured on 2026-09-24 in a worktree of SorraAgents. See `docs/dev/find-related-v3-analysis.md` and `skill/find-related/SKILL.md`.

## AC verification

| AC | Verdict | Evidence |
|----|---------|----------|
| Confirm v3 merged & deployed | Met | `git log dev` contains `50518097 perf(find-related): v3 speed & value … (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9)`. All three related items are terminal: SA-0MS3CIU1400272WT (completed/done), SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH (completed/done), SA-0MS7FO6TO001ZBF0 (completed/done). |
| Verify <5s on representative items | Partially met | Warm runs: **5.28s, 5.62s** (exceeds <5s); first cold run: 9.85s. Phase breakdown: `wl show` 0.32s; semantic probe 0.45s; **8 sequential `wl search` 3.43s** (~0.43s each); repo scan (421 files) 0.34s; `wl update` 0.39s. Follow-up: SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ. |
| Reports compact & useful | Met (compactness) | Description report caps keyword lists at 5 with `(+N more)`; `MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS=3`, `MAX_REPO_FILE_RESULTS=3`. Full untruncated report persisted to `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-<id>.md`. Relevance is weak — see SA-0MUG46NJE003JOCD. |
| Idempotency | Met | Two consecutive runs produced byte-identical descriptions (SHA-256 `b4489eee…`, report section length 887 both times). Single `## Related work (automated report)` section; no stacked `###` blocks. |
| Document remaining issues | Met | This comment + SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ, SA-0MUG46NJE003JOCD, SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4, SA-0MUG47DYG006TV40. |

## What v3 fixed (confirmed)

- **Search fan-out**: 8 subprocesses (top-`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), not 523. Observed 8 `wl search --semantic` calls.
- **Feedback loop closed**: `extract_keywords` strips the automated-report section before tokenising; report tokens never re-enter the keyword set.
- **Repo scan noise removed**: `.worklog`, `.pi`, cache dirs excluded; scan found 421 files (vs 2,188 pre-v3) and never matches the sidecar.
- **Idempotency boundary fix**: `
##(?!#)` boundary keeps `###` sub-headings inside the section; re-runs replace atomically.

## Remaining issues (tracked separately)

1. **Runtime >5s** — per-subprocess latency of 8 sequential searches dominates. Parallelising (or reducing the cap) should bring it under target. → SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ (task, medium).
2. **Weak keyword relevance** — top-8 frequency-ranked terms are corpus-generic (`skill, related, work, find, report, improvements, item, keyword`); 2 of 3 related items are unrelated C401 lint items and repo matches are audit docs. No IDF/title weighting. → SA-0MUG46NJE003JOCD (task, medium).
3. **Misleading verbose output** — `--verbose` prints all 155 extracted keywords, but only the top 8 are searched; JSON exposes only the full list. → SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4 (task, low).
4. **Test-infra recursion** (found while validating this review) — a cold-cache/concurrent full-suite run can recurse: `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` spawns a real `audit_runner.py issue` child which auto-executes the real full suite. Observed 19-50+ nested processes and a 1500s timeout. The suite passes sequentially on a warm cache (350s, success). → SA-0MUG47DYG006TV40 (bug, high).

## Changes made by this review

- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — corrected the runtime expectation to "~3–6s" and added a machine-variance note (the v3 analysis measured ~3s on a faster machine). Commit `2777c7e1`.

## Constraints honoured

- Review was evidence-driven (measured wall-clock, subprocess counts, repo-scan counts, idempotency hashes).
- v3 changes were not re-implemented.
- Further improvements are separate work items (above).

Investigation findings:

- In this repository (/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents), I found no source path that explicitly deletes <project>/.worklog/ampa/.env. The tracked AMPA runtime code is not present here; this repo mostly references AMPA installer/runtime externally.
- The active AMPA plugin runtime at /home/rgardler/.config/opencode/.worklog/plugins/ampa.mjs also does not contain direct deletion of .worklog/ampa/.env.
- I found a concrete destructive path in the AMPA installer script used in local installs (external source at /home/rgardler/projects/ampa/skill/install-ampa/scripts/install-worklog-plugin.sh): copy_python_package() executes rm -rf "/ampa" during upgrades, which removes ampa_py/ampa/.env unless restore succeeds.
- Historical install decision logs show repeated .env backups to /tmp/ampa_env_backups/.env.preinstall.* without corresponding restore entries for that .env backup, while scheduler_store restore entries are present. Evidence files:
  - /tmp/ampa_install_decisions.27742
  - /tmp/ampa_install_decisions.23495
  - /tmp/ampa_install_decisions.31728
  - backup artifacts still present under /tmp/ampa_env_backups/.env.preinstall.*
- This indicates a real, reproducible upgrade path where the installed AMPA .env is removed during reinstall/upgrade and not restored by the installer version that produced those logs.

Most likely root cause: installer upgrade flow removing ampa_py/ampa tree during copy and failing to restore backed-up .env in certain installed versions.

Q2: "CI policy for dev (blocking checks) - Which checks should be required on dev before a human may approve a merge to main?"
- Options: A) Smoke+critical on dev; B) Full test-suite on every dev push; C) Smoke+critical on dev and automated full-suite pre-merge.
- Answer (user): "C" — Smoke + critical tests on dev per-change, and an automated full test-suite run that must pass before main merge.
- Answering party: user (interactive reply). Source: planning session.
- Final: C

Q3: "Human approval / merge trigger - Who should be able to perform the final dev→main merge and how is it triggered?"
- Options: A) Any maintainer/reviewer; B) Designated release manager; C) Require explicit Producer sign-off OR named reviewer + manual trigger.
- Answer (user): "B" — A designated release manager triggers the merge.
- Answering party: user (interactive reply). Source: planning session.
- Final: B

OPEN QUESTION: "Do you want a hard enforcement mechanism (server-side branch protection or hook) that prevents pushes to main in addition to agent-side checks?"
- Why it matters: server-side enforcement reduces risk of accidental direct pushes to main; agent-side checks alone are weaker.
- Suggested options: Yes (add branch protection rules and server-side hooks) / No (rely on agent-side policy + human review).
- Status: OPEN — awaiting product/operator decision.
